# Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

Format: [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/)

## [V3.925] — 2026-10-26 — Deploys are encrypted: FTP over verified TLS, never a plain-FTP fallback

Found by Gabe's Claude on his first FTP setup: the GoDaddy FTP server (Pure-FTPd, 198.12.245.91) presents a valid certificate for `*.prod.phx3.secureserver.net`, never for mcgheelab.com, so the TLS handshake failed on the hostname check and `ftp_connect` (`"tls": "auto"`) fell back to **plain FTP — on every deploy, the lab's included, with the password in the clear**. Reproduced here: `mcgheelab.com` → `SSLCertVerificationError: Hostname mismatch`. The server's own name, `p3plzcpnl504220.prod.phx3.secureserver.net` (cPanel Server Name; also the Exim banner on 587), resolves to the same IP and verifies fully (TLS 1.3).

### Bug Fixes
- `scripts/deploy.py` `ftp_connect`: connects by `tls_host(f)` — `ftp.tlsHost` when set, after checking it resolves to the same address as `ftp.host` (a server move raises "the site has moved servers… set tlsHost", instead of logging in to another machine); `host` stays the site's name because the macOS Keychain entry is filed under it. With `"tls": "always"` a TLS failure raises `RuntimeError("TLS failed and plain FTP is off …")` (plus a certifi hint for "self-signed certificate in certificate chain" / "local issuer") and nothing is sent.
- `deploy/site.json` `ftp`: `"tls": "always"`, `"tlsHost": "p3plzcpnl504220.prod.phx3.secureserver.net"`.
- `ssl_context()`: certifi's roots are added whenever certifi is installed, not only when the default store is empty — Windows fills its root store lazily, so Python there can lack GoDaddy's root (Gabe's "self-signed certificate in certificate chain").

### Added
- `python3 scripts/deploy.py check` (`cmd_check`): log in, `NLST` the remote root over the data channel, print the transport and whether the login lands on the web root (`index.html`, `rm`, `sw.js`); uploads nothing. Run here: `McGheeLab@mcgheelab.com at p3plzcpnl504220… via FTPS (explicit TLS)`, `OK: / is the web root`. With `tlsHost` removed it refuses (hostname mismatch) and with `tlsHost` on another machine it refuses (moved), both before any login. An upload (`STOR`) over TLS was not exercised here; the next site change's auto-deploy is the first.

### Changed
- `deploy/README.md` (the `check` row; TLS only, `tlsHost`, Cyberduck), `scientia/SETUP.md` (certifi in the tools; step 5 uses `deploy.py check`, TLS only, the two errors and what they mean), `scientia/CLAUDE.md` FTP row.

## [V3.924] — 2026-10-26 — The end-of-turn auto-push pushes a new branch; a setup page for Gabe's Windows PC

### Bug Fixes
- `scripts/git_autopush.py` never pushed a branch origin did not have yet: `git fetch origin <branch>` failed ("couldn't find remote ref") and the turn ended "could not reach origin — commit kept locally", every turn, so Gabe's `scientia/<topic>` branches (scientia/CLAUDE.md, V3.868) reached GitHub only by a hand push. Now a failed fetch asks `git ls-remote --exit-code --heads origin <branch>`: exit 2 (origin answers, no such branch) sets `new_branch`, skips the rebase, counts what origin has on no branch (`rev-list HEAD --not --remotes=origin`), runs the push gate from `merge-base HEAD origin/<deployBranch>` against `origin/<deployBranch>` (what the pull request merges into; before, a missing `origin/<branch>` fell back to the root commit, i.e. the whole history), and pushes with `-u` ("pushed … (new branch)"). Any other failure (offline, auth) is still "could not reach origin". `scripts/tests/merge_check_test.py`: 5 new fixtures (36/36) — a new branch pushed on its first turn, origin has it, it tracks it, its next turn is an ordinary push, an unreachable origin keeps the commit local; the first four fail on the old script.

### Added
- `scientia/SETUP.md`: setting up the repo on Gabe's Windows PC the way Alex's Mac works — tools (Python reachable as `python3`, since the Stop hooks, pre-push hook and manifest merge driver call it by that name and the hooks swallow a failure), `core.autocrlf false` before cloning (a CRLF checkout differs byte for byte from `deploy/manifest.json` and the first auto-deploy would re-upload most of the site) + `files.eol`, `gh auth login` / `setup-git`, the once-per-clone steps with a CRLF check and a `deploy.py status` sanity check, how the hook pushes a branch, and FTP: `scripts/.env` with his own login (`gabe@mcgheelab.com`, made 2026-10-26), a connection test that confirms the login lands on the web root, deploy only from `main`.

### Changed
- `scientia/CLAUDE.md`: links SETUP.md from the Git workflow section; the FTP access row says the account exists; the hook pushes Gabe's branch every turn, a new one included.

## [V3.922] — 2026-10-26 — The repo clones on Windows again: two junk file names removed, and the push gate refuses a name Windows cannot check out

Gabe's clone on Windows (GitHub Desktop) stopped with `error: invalid path '~65ZT?2WlbSZ copy.txt'` / `fatal: unable to checkout working tree`: Windows forbids `?` in a file name, and git stops the checkout at the first such path, leaving no working tree.

### Changed
- `scripts/merge_check.py`: `check_paths(rep, head, files)` runs on every range (pre-push hook, `git_autopush.py`, the GitHub Action) and HOLDs a new path a Windows clone cannot check out. `windows_problem(path)`: a component holding `< > : " \ | ? *` or a control character, ending in a dot or space, or named `CON` / `PRN` / `AUX` / `NUL` / `COM1-9` / `LPT1-9` (with or without an extension); plus a path that differs only in case from another in the tree (`git ls-tree -r` at the head, `git ls-files` for `worktree`). `unquote(path)` undoes git's C-quoting first, so a quoted non-ASCII name is not mistaken for one containing `"` or `\`. Checked against `791bda16` (it adds `~65ZT?2WlbSZ copy.txt`): HELD.

### Bug Fixes
- Removed `~65ZT?2WlbSZ.txt` (added in "repo moved") and `~65ZT?2WlbSZ copy.txt` (V3.868) from the repo root: both empty, referenced nowhere. They were the only tracked paths Windows rejects (no reserved names, case collisions or long paths; the longest path is 82 characters).

## [V3.921] — 2026-10-26 — Paper builder: PLOS pages as PLOS prints them — the first-page article-information sidebar, masthead, running head and foot

Plan: [CodeLog/ClaudesPlan/V3.921_plos_sidebar_furniture.md](../ClaudesPlan/V3.921_plos_sidebar_furniture.md).

Asked why every PLOS page has its text "shifted over". Measured 25 PLOS ONE / Biology / Computational Biology PDFs (2015–2024): PLOS sets the body at x = 200 bp on every page (the look already did); what was missing is what PLOS prints in that margin and around the page.

### Added
- `look.sidebar` (`rm/js/paper-look.js`): the first-page article-information column — "OPEN ACCESS", Citation, Copyright, Data Availability Statement, Funding, Competing interests — Helvetica Condensed 8/11 bp at x 36–184, bottom-aligned on page 1 (last baseline 709, first no higher than 353.6), continued at the top of page 2 (first baseline 83.3). `PaperLook.sidebarSplit(look, sections)` takes the three statements OUT of the body (a section by name or special key — `data_availability`, `funding`, `competing_interests` — or a back-matter paragraph opening with that bold run-in label); `PaperLook.sidebarItems(look, info)` writes the Citation ("Surname Initials", six names then "et al.", year, title, journal) and Copyright (CC-BY) paragraphs; a statement the paper lacks says to add it before submission.
- PDF: `PaperLook.texSidebar` sets the column in one `\vbox` (first baseline one `\baselineskip` below its top, no penalties, `\exhyphenpenalty=0`, no interword shrink, fil ragged right — the browser's greedy line count) and `\vsplit`s it at page 1's span; `PaperLook.texFurniture` writes `\rmPageFurniture`, drawn by `\AddToHook{shipout/background}` at absolute positions (body flow untouched). Tokens `{{RM_PAGE_FURNITURE}}` / `{{RM_SIDEBAR}}` in a look's main.tex.
- `look.furniture` `{first, head, foot}`: items `{text, x | right, y (baseline), size, weight}` with `{journal}`, `{short_title}`, `{page}`, `{pages}` (lastpage). PLOS: masthead (20.6 bp, baseline 48.3) and "RESEARCH ARTICLE" (101.4) on page 1; journal + short title (46.2) on later pages; journal and "n / N" at every foot (756). `PaperLook.journalName(look, target)` — the paper's target journal when it matches `look.journal_family`, else `journal_default`; `PaperLook.shortTitle(title)`.
- Document view: `_mountFurniture` / `_alignFurniture` (each line placed on its measured baseline — Chrome snaps baselines to whole pixels) and `_mountSidebar` (same paragraphs, split at the last line whose baseline fits, clipped copies on pages 1 and 2); the grey "n / ≈N" counter hides on a sheet that prints its own folio.
- Font: TeX Gyre Heros Condensed (`rm/vendor/fonts/texgyreheroscn-*.otf`, GUST licence, from the Tectonic bundle) as `PaperLook.FONTS['heros-cn']`.
- `paper-export.js` passes `targetJournal` to `buildBundle`.
- `scripts/tests/paper-look-furniture.test.mjs` (50 checks).

### Changed
- PLOS look: `title.before: 36` — page 1's front starts under the masthead and "RESEARCH ARTICLE" (title baseline 125.4; PLOS 124–126); `footer.page_numbers: false` (the furniture prints the folio). `texFront` writes `title.before` as `\vspace*{before − \topskip}\nointerlineskip` (exactly `before`, as the view's margin).
- Every spec look's front matter is rigid in the PDF (`\parskip=0pt` inside `\rmfront`; `\lineskiplimit=-\maxdimen` in the title, author and affiliation lines only — a boxed abstract keeps `\lineskip`, or it rides up over the affiliations): a first page cut short no longer has `\flushbottom` pull the title, authors and abstract apart, and an author superscript under a title descender no longer adds TeX's `\lineskip` (~2 bp the view did not have). Case study page 1: abstract 6.1 bp → 0.3 bp from the view.
- Document view packer models TeX's shrink (`_packPages`: `shrinkOf`, `stretchOf`, `prefersOver`, `splitRoom`): a block or one more line that overshoots the column fits when the page's shrinkable glue covers it (heading skip `minus 1bp` — none after a fixed skip, `\addvspace` keeps the larger — display skips 3 bp each side, list `\topsep` 1 bp, in-text float 2 bp) AND TeX's page builder would rather shrink than stretch (badness 100·(amount/glue)³ either way). `_flushBottoms` takes the overshoot back out of the same gaps (`shrinkGaps`). A 7-line paragraph 0.46 px too tall had moved to the next page leaving six lines of room (PLOS ground truth p. 11).
- Document view: the PLOS bibliography as plos2015.bst sets it (`_formatPlos`: "Surname Initials", six then "et al.", journal without dots, "Year;Vol(Num):pages" / ";p. pages", no DOI) instead of the generic numeric format, which ran longer and added a page.

### Bug Fixes
- PDF: under a heading-style abstract label (PLOS) the abstract's first line was indented by `\parindent` (the view sets it flush, as PLOS prints it) and could run a line longer; abstract paragraphs are flush (`\parindent` = `abstract.first_indent`, 0).
- Document view: a table cell's typesetting width was read just before that cell was set — a typeset cell reflows its table, so later rows were measured wider and the same text stayed on one line there while it broke in rows 1–2 (and in every row of the PDF). All widths are read first (`_typesetParagraphs`).
- `scripts/paper-lab/sync.py` crashed (KeyError) when a matched line's first character did not map (running head / sidebar text beside it).
- Document view: a heading kept only two lines of a following block it could not break (a table set in the text) and stood alone at the foot of a page while the PDF carried both over; `keepNextH` is now the whole block when TeX cannot break it (`_splits` false and shorter than half a page).

## [V3.920] — 2026-10-26 — Paper builder: a full case-study paper set cleanly — equations, lists, footnotes, tables, references, in page view and PDF

Plan: [CodeLog/ClaudesPlan/V3.920_case_study_formatting.md](../ClaudesPlan/V3.920_case_study_formatting.md).

### Bug Fixes
- Document view: display equations were drawn about 1.5 lines too high, over the text above (`_setDisplays` measured KaTeX's baseline with a marker that fell below `.katex-html`, a block in display mode; now inside the first `.base`, after `.pdv-eq-tex` applies). A display that would run into its number shifts left or sets the number on its own line (amsmath).
- PDF: panel references with an unprefixed label (`[!fig:system:C]`, the paper-bundle format) compiled to `\ref{system:C}` — "Fig. ??". Math inside the paper's own `\textbf{…}` / `\emph{…}` printed "0" (nested placeholders were reinserted in one pass). A list item opening with "[" became `\item`'s optional label (`\item {}[`).
- PDF: a reference missing from the library printed "% @misc … data/items.json …"; it is now a real entry reading "Reference not in the lab library: KEY — add it before submission" (same words in the Document view).
- Document view: footnotes in a two-column look sit at the foot of the column holding their mark, with their room reserved (`c.notes`, split parts keep the notes whose marks they hold, `_notesIn`); notes are read from the `[^…]` source and set as prose ("(click to edit)" printed before); `\footnotesize` at the look's leading under a 40% rule.
- Document view: lists break across columns and pages between items or typeset lines (`_splitList`; numbering continues via `start`, a cut item has no second marker); a longtable in the text breaks between rows (`_splitTableRows`), also when it is taller than a fresh page.
- Document view: a waiting page-wide table no longer holds back a figure (or a figure a table) — floats keep order per type, as LaTeX does. A run-in heading waits over a float for the paragraph that follows. In one column, an imported `tabular` / `longtable` outside a `table` float sits in the text, as in the PDF.
- Tables: the natural width (column or page) is measured on the body rows — a header may wrap — in `\rmTnat` and `_tableNaturalW`. Math and the text touching it ("(µm)") never break apart in cells (`_nowrapCellMath`); a source newline in a cell is a space; a bare `p{}` column of an imported table is justified and hyphenated (`parseTabular().justify`).
- References: `PaperCiteStyle` numbering and `getCitedKeysInPaper` read `\cite{…}` written in the paper's own LaTeX, list blocks and imported tables, so the Document view's numbers and list match the PDF; the look's label ("(1)" ACS, "[1]", "1."), and achemso's entry format for ACS (`_formatAchemso`).
- Float pages spread their floats (`\@fpsep`) instead of stacking them in the middle.

### Changed
- Lists in every spec look are set compactly, as journals set them: `\@listi` / `\@listii` with `\topsep` 3bp, `\itemsep` 1bp, no `\partopsep`, 1.5em indent (`PaperLook.listSpacing`; `look.list` overrides), and the Document view's list CSS reads the same numbers.
- IEEE look: tables in `\footnotesize` as IEEEtran sets them (`look.table`; `\rmTable` measures at that size), "TABLE II" with the caption in small caps centred under it (`caption.table_style: 'ieee'`, `table_numbering: 'Roman'`, also in "(continued)" lines and reference chips), "1)" enumerate labels and IEEEtran's list spacing (`look.list`).
- 3 tests in `paper-tex-escape.test.mjs` (panel refs), 3 more (math in `\textbf`, `\emph`, an item opening with "[") — 57 checks.

## [V3.919] — 2026-10-25 — Paper builder: every page filled to the foot — no text hanging over white space

Plan: [CodeLog/ClaudesPlan/V3.919_pages_filled_to_the_foot.md](../ClaudesPlan/V3.919_pages_filled_to_the_foot.md).

### Changed
- PDF: every page is filled to the bottom margin (`\flushbottom`) in every journal look (`paper-look.js` `texPreamble`: was `\raggedbottom` for PLOS, NSF and the numeric preprint; class looks set it at `\AtBeginDocument`) and in templates without a look (`paper-export-tex.js` appends it to the preamble). Room a page cannot use — a heading kept with its first lines, a float that went on — is spread through the page's glue instead of being left at the foot. Spec looks write `\parskip … plus 1bp` (LaTeX's own default; it was fixed): a column of plain paragraphs had nothing to stretch, so the room stayed at the foot, or all of it went into the one float gap on the page (NSF p. 7 under Figure 4). Grant looks keep their rigid headings (wrapfig).
- PDF: an imported figure or table written to stay "here" (`[H]`, `[h]`, `[h!]`) floats under a journal look (`_floatRawTex` → `[tbp]`, starred `[tp]`); `[H]` ended the page early whenever the float did not fit. Built figures and tables already float under a look; an explicit Lock keeps its place.
- Document view: `_flushBottoms()` after mounting does what `\flushbottom` does — the room under each column's (or one-column page's) text goes into the gaps between its blocks in proportion to TeX's stretch there — what follows the block above plus what precedes the block below (`\parskip` 1, titlesec heading 2 + 1 (+ parskip), rigid grant headings 0, display 2 / 2, list 2 + parskip / 2, in-text float 2 / 2, none after a display); a float at the foot keeps its `\textfloatsep` share, as `padding-top` so collapsing margins cannot absorb it. Not on the last text page (except a full left column) nor before a forced break (`page.noFlush`, a stand-alone front page). Sheets carry `data-flush`.
- Document view tables under a look: a wrapping or `p{}` cell gets 1 pt more on its right (TeX shrinks interword space to keep a line a hair too long; "Numerical Aperture", 82.1 pt in an 82 pt column, is one line in the PDF and wrapped here, which cost the PLOS paper a page).

## [V3.918] — 2026-10-25 — Paper builder: tables set the way journals set them — across the page when too wide for a column, continued when longer than a page

Plan: [CodeLog/ClaudesPlan/V3.918_tables_journal_width.md](../ClaudesPlan/V3.918_tables_journal_width.md).

### Changed
- Tables in a two-column layout follow the journal rule (Alex: "journals … do full width for tables unless the table is small enough to fit within a column"). A table stays in one column only when its **natural width** — set without wrapping, each column as wide as its widest cell, fixed columns (`p{3cm}`, a width in mm) at their width, and a column that wraps when printed counted at most a third of the column (prose may wrap: the JACS abbreviation list, one long meaning, stays in its column as in the published article) — fits one; otherwise it is set across the page. Every table used to be created with `span:'column'`, so that stored value now means "decide" (`PaperLayout.tableSpan(attrs)` → `'auto' | 'column' | 'page'`); the Table layout popover offers Fit / One column (`span:'one-column'`) / Full page width, and new tables store `span:'auto'`.
- A table taller than the page continues on the next page(s), headed "Table N (continued)" with its header rows repeated; the caption stays on the first piece, notes on the last (longtable cannot run in two columns).
- PDF export (`paper-export-tex.js`): in two-column layouts every table goes through `\rmTable` (new preamble macros, `RM_TABLE_TEX`, injected on use). TeX measures the natural form (`\rmTnat`; a wrapping column's cells clipped to `\columnwidth/3` by `\rmTcellA`/`\rmTcellB`, an `lrbox`) against `\columnwidth` to choose `table` / `table*`, then measures each row at the printed width and starts a new float when `\textheight` less the caption and header is full. A table that fits makes one float exactly as before. `tableToTex`'s per-row cell code is now `rowCellsTex(r)`, shared by both paths (one-column output byte-identical).
- Imported LaTeX tables (`attrs.raw_tex`) in two-column layouts are taken apart by `PaperProseTex.splitTable(raw)` (env, spec, size/spacing setup, caption + label + position, outer rules, header rows, each body row with the rules above it; a longtable's `\endfirsthead` / `\endhead` give the header and its footers are dropped) and set by `\rmTable` — so an imported longtable now compiles in two columns. Anything else (`tabularx`, `\resizebox`, threeparttable, a `#`) stays verbatim.
- Document view (`paper-doc-view.js`): `_layoutTables(items, geom)` runs once the look's CSS and fonts are on the probe (before `_measureItems`): `_tableNaturalW` measures the natural width (`.pdv-tbl-natural`), `_tablePieces` cuts a too-tall table at row boundaries with TeX's limit; pieces are separate floats (`data-piece`, part of the measure-cache key).
- Document view tables under a journal look are set as TeX sets a tabular, so they break where the PDF breaks them (`paper-look.js` CSS): body size, `\tabcolsep` padding, one look leading per row, booktabs rule spacing, density as `\arraystretch`, plain header row, whole words (an unbreakable word sticks out like TeX's overfull box instead of adding lines), the caption above the table when the look says so (`.pdv-tabcap-above`; imported tables keep their source's position). Cells top-aligned everywhere (`\multirow` centred).
- Imported tables in the Document view keep LaTeX's columns: `p{…}` widths (with the cell padding TeX adds outside them), `l/c/r` unwrapped (`.pdv-tbl-tex`), `\multicolumn` spans as merged cells, the source's size step (`\scriptsize` 70 %, was a flat 90 %).

### Bug Fixes
- `parseTabular`: `\multicolumn{7}{@{}l}{…}` (braces in the alignment) printed as source in the Document view; a longtable printed its `\endhead` / repeated header / footer rows as data.
- An imported table without a `\caption` took a table number in the builder and the Document view; TeX does not number it, so every later table was off by one (`getAllTables`).
- An imported `longtable` in a one-column template failed to compile ("Environment longtable undefined"): `packagesFor` loads `longtable` (and `array` for `>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}`) when the paper's LaTeX uses them.

## [V3.917] — 2026-10-25 — Paper builder: lists inside paragraphs and hard-wrapped text set correctly in journal looks

Plan: [CodeLog/ClaudesPlan/V3.917_lists_and_soft_breaks.md](../ClaudesPlan/V3.917_lists_and_soft_breaks.md).

### Bug Fixes
- A paragraph holding "- item" lines (lead-in sentence + list, the ME3B paper's Design requirements) printed its items over each other with stray "- •" markers under a journal look: the typesetter set the whole paragraph, list included, as one run of text, cutting lines through the `<ul>` so every cut line became its own bullet and the hyphen it appends at a break landed beside it. `paper-doc-view.js` `_buildBlockNode` now returns such a paragraph as consecutive page items (`more`): prose → typeset paragraph, list → `.pdv-list-block` (`_listItemsHtml`, shared with list blocks), prose after a list → `pdv-noindent pdv-para-cont` (the PDF's continuation after `itemize`). The page may break between them.
- Words ran together where the source had a line break inside a paragraph ("adding the" / "ME3B" → "theME3B", "compatiblecondenser", "workingdistance"): the Document view rendered `\n` as `<br>`. LaTeX reads a single newline as a space, so the page view does too now (`softBreaks`; a blank line still breaks, list lines keep theirs).
- `paper-typeset.js` `breakLines`: a forced break inside a paragraph (`<br>`, EJECT) ended the pass, dropping every word after it; only the paragraph's final EJECT ends it now. New test in `paper-typeset.test.mjs` (fails on the old code).
- `paper-typeset.js`: U+2028/U+2029, vertical tab and NEL (pasted text) are word spaces; they glued neighbouring words together.
- PDF export: bold text holding an *italic* span ("**S1 Dataset. … along *z* …**") printed stray asterisks in every journal format — the bold pattern refused any `*` inside. `paragraphTextToTex` now allows whole italic spans inside bold (`/\*\*((?:[^*\n]|\*[^*\n]+\*)+)\*\*/`); 2 tests in `paper-tex-escape.test.mjs`. Found in the PLOS corpus paper's supporting-information captions.

### Changed
- List items (list blocks and paragraph lists) are typeset under a journal look — justified, hyphenated and broken by Knuth–Plass like the PDF's `itemize` (`TYPESET_INNER_SEL` gains `.pdv-list-block li`; an item holding a nested list keeps browser layout). They were ragged right.

## [V3.916] — 2026-10-25 — Open RM tabs follow each deploy; compiles show their wait and (after a redeploy) start warm

Plan: [CodeLog/ClaudesPlan/V3.916_stale_tabs_and_compile_wait.md](../ClaudesPlan/V3.916_stale_tabs_and_compile_wait.md).

### Added
- `rm/js/build-check.js` (`window.RM_BUILD`): compares `/rm/build.json` with the stamp the page started with — at start, on visibility → visible, focus, `online`, every 5 min. New stamp → `location.reload()` when the tab is hidden or was just brought back and nothing is held, else a bottom bar (Reload / Later). Held: focused input/textarea/select/contenteditable, a live `MediaRecorder` or `getUserMedia` stream (both wrapped to watch), `window.RM_HOLD_RELOAD`. Off on localhost/`*.local` and in frames. Loaded by `runtime-mode.js` (deploy mode) and a direct tag on the 20 RM pages without it.
- `scripts/deploy.py` `stamp_build(changed, files, idx)`: an upload that changes site files rewrites `rm/build.json` (`{build, head, sw, files}`) and sends it last (`ftp`, `stage`, `autodeploy`). Git-ignored.
- `scripts/paper-lab/warmup.py`: a synthetic paper compiled through the real Export page for every template and page look → `functions/paper-compile/warmup/papers.tar.gz`; the names of every bundle file fetched compiling that set and every Paper Lab paper → `warmup/tex-files.txt` (485 files, 27 MB of cache). `--list-only` rebuilds the list.
- `scripts/paper-lab/drive.mjs compile` records what the page shows after the response (`compile-after.json`: status, viewer pages).

### Changed
- `functions/paper-compile/Dockerfile`: `TECTONIC_CACHE_DIR=/opt/tectonic-cache`, filled at build time (`tectonic -X bundle cat` over `tex-files.txt`, then the warm-up papers compiled once). Needs a Cloud Run redeploy; README carries the command (`--timeout 120`, the live service had 90).
- `paper-export.js` `_compileAction`: elapsed-seconds status, a cold-server note in the log, `_pdfLink(url)` (Open PDF) as soon as the response arrives, `AbortController` at `COMPILE_TIMEOUT_MS` (180 s) with a message.

### Bug Fixes
- An RM tab opened before a deploy kept running the old build until reloaded by hand (the root SPA reloads on the worker's `controllerchange`; RM pages never listened) — the "still wrong after the fix went live" reports.
- Compile PDF showed nothing between "Sending bundle…" and the PDF — 47 s on a cold Cloud Run instance, which read as a hang.
- The Export page failed to open ("`(a.affiliationIdx || []).map is not a function`") for an author with one affiliation stored as a number (the paper-bundle skill's example format); the PDF and the Document view dropped that affiliation. All readers accept a number or a list (`paper-export-config.js`, `paper-export-tex.js`, `paper-doc-view.js`); the skill example writes `[0]`.
- `paper-look.js` `applyToTemplate`: under a published look a class environment in `section_kind_to_command` (APS's `acknowledgments`) is an unnumbered section, as special sections already were — APS papers with Acknowledgements failed to compile.

## [V3.915] — 2026-10-25 — Paper builder: LaTeX written in prose (papers imported from .tex) in the preview and the PDF

Plan: [CodeLog/ClaudesPlan/V3.915_prose_latex_imported_papers.md](../ClaudesPlan/V3.915_prose_latex_imported_papers.md).

### Added
- `rm/js/paper-prose-tex.js` (`window.PaperProseTex`, pure): `readCommand(s, i)`, `tildeAt(s, i)` (subscript / tie / character), `unitHtml` / `numHtml` (siunitx), `toHtml(cmd, ctx)` (Document view), `toTex(cmd, ctx)` (export: verbatim, references and citations per template, `false` = unknown → text), `packagesFor(tex)` / `preambleLoads(preamble, pkg)`, `parseTabular(raw)`, `decodeAccents(s)`. Loaded by paper-builder.html and paper-export.html before paper-export-tex.js.
- `scripts/tests/paper-prose-tex.test.mjs` (50 checks, in run-all.sh); `paper-tex-escape.test.mjs` +10 (MEBP phrases, cref, unknown macros, BibTeX accents).
- `scripts/paper-lab/drive.mjs preview … --probe FILE`: evaluates a JS expression in the page after layout → `probe.json`.

### Changed
- `paper-editor.js` `renderParagraphHtml`: a `\` starts a LaTeX command read by `PaperProseTex` (`_proseTexCtx`: references through the figure/table/equation/section chips, `\ref` as the bare number, citations and footnotes through their chips); `~` follows `tildeAt` (tie → U+00A0). Display only — focused paragraphs still show their source.
- `paper-export-tex.js` `paragraphTextToTex`: `_protectProseTex` after the inline-math pass — known commands go to LaTeX as written (the pre-V3.906 behaviour), `\cref`/`\Cref` become the template's prefix + `\ref` unless cleveref is on, unknown commands are escaped as text; the `~x~` regex pass is replaced by `tildeAt`. `buildBundle` adds siunitx / cleveref / booktabs / float / ulem to the preamble when the paper's own LaTeX needs them. `collectCitationKeys` reads `\cite{…}` (prose and `raw_tex`). `bibEscape` decodes BibTeX accents first and escapes `$` and `^`.
- `paper-doc-view.js`: a table block with only `attrs.raw_tex` is drawn from `PaperProseTex.parseTabular` (rows, alignment, midrules, `\small`, caption); an unknown figure/table/equation reference prints "Fig. ??" (label on the tooltip); the preview bibliography decodes BibTeX accents (`_decodeEntryAccents`).
- `paper-editor.js` `getAllFigures` / `getAllTables`: `label` falls back to the `\label{}` in `raw_tex` (`_rawTexLabel`).

### Bug Fixes
- Imported papers printed `\si{\micro\metre}`, `\cref{fig:x}`, `\%` as code in the Document view, and (since V3.906's escaping) in the PDF.
- `[X]~\si{…} (n~=~[X])` was read as one long `~subscript~`: half a sentence set as a tiny unbreakable box that ran into the margin and overprinted the next line, and `\textsubscript{…}` in the PDF. LaTeX ties are now no-break spaces; `H~2~O` is still a subscript.
- `paper-typeset.js` `layoutParagraph`: a line lying wholly inside a `<strong>`/`<em>`/`<sub>` lost that element (`Range.cloneContents` keeps only the elements the range cuts through) — bold run-in heads printed plain, the middle lines of a long italic passage upright. Each line is re-wrapped in shallow copies of its ancestors up to the paragraph.
- An imported LaTeX table previewed as an empty "Table 1."
- The mebp-journal PDF stopped at the bibliography ("Missing $ inserted") on a BibTeX accent in an author name.
- Cross-reference chips in the Document view: the editor's `inline-block` survived the sheet flattening, so a justified line padded "(Fig. ??)" apart; chips are `display: inline` on the page now. The journal prefix is tied to the number with a no-break space (`_rewriteRefPrefixes`), so "Fig." and its number never split across lines — the PDF's `Fig.~\ref{…}`.

Plan: [CodeLog/ClaudesPlan/V3.911_nsf_grant_format.md](../ClaudesPlan/V3.911_nsf_grant_format.md).

### Added
- **Document** picker in the Document view toolbar (`#pdv-doc`, `_syncDocPicker`), shown for a template with a `grant.documents` list: Project Description, References Cited, Project Summary, Data Management and Sharing Plan, Mentoring Plan, Synergistic Activities, Budget Justification, Facilities, Departmental Letter. `state.grantDoc` selects one; `renderDocument` sets it in the grant's look with the title hidden (`PaperLook.merge(look, {title:{show:false}})`), its kinds mapped to `section_star`, the tree filtered to those kinds; References Cited (`references:true`) renders the bibliography alone (`state.subdocRefs` overrides `bib.where:'separate'`). The page meter, the Check panel rules and Fit follow the chosen document's limit. An empty document shows how to add it.
- **Grant documents** card on the Export page (`_bindGrantDocs`, `PaperSubdocs.grantDocs` / `buildGrantDocBundle`): one row per document with its limit, `.zip` and **Compile**, and the last PDF of that document. Compiles carry `templateId: '<template>#<doc>'` and `docKind: 'grant_<doc>'`; `mainCompiles()` drops `#` templates, so a References Cited compile never stands in for the Project Description (the deployed compile service files unknown docKinds as `main`).

### Changed
- `paper-import-engine.js`: a grant-document section (`GRANT_ATTACHED_KINDS`) with written text stays a section on import; uploaded PDFs still go to Grant Docs.
- `functions/paper-compile/server.js` accepts `docKind: 'grant_<doc>'` (takes effect with the next Cloud Run deploy of paper-compile; until then the client's `#` tag keeps these compiles out of the main history).

### Bug Fixes
- The preview bibliography printed the citation key as the author of an author-less reference ("anon2022fda"); now nothing, and the entry starts at its title.
- Journal looks (found chasing bioRxiv's lost page): the paginator added an item's top and bottom margins in full, but adjoining spaces count once, the larger (CSS collapses them; LaTeX's `\addvspace` does the same), and TeX discards the space before an item at the top of a page or column. `runEff` / `runPut` (one column) and `colEff` / `colPut` (two) now do both, with the margins kept per measured item (`x.mt`, `x.mb`, also in the measure cache). PLOS: 13 / 14 → 13 / 13 pages.
- Journal looks: display equations were spaced by KaTeX's own 1em margins on top of the look's — about a line and a half too tall each. `_setDisplays` sets each from TeX's display rules (\abovedisplayskip / short skips by the line above, interline glue against KaTeX's strut height and depth at the body size, \belowdisplayskip, an empty line for a display that starts a paragraph) and puts the math on TeX's baseline.
- Templates that compile with unsrtnat (NSF, preprint-numeric) show their bibliography in unsrtnat's format in the preview (`_formatUnsrtnat`: every author, BibTeX's sentence case, `vol (num):pages, year`, `doi:`); the editor's citation entries now carry up to 80 authors (was 10).

## [V3.913] — 2026-10-25 — Grants: page budget, the PAPPG rules and Fit in the Check panel

Plan: [CodeLog/ClaudesPlan/V3.911_nsf_grant_format.md](../ClaudesPlan/V3.911_nsf_grant_format.md).

### Added
- Check panel, grant section (`_grantPanelHtml`, `_grantReport`): **pages / limit** with the lines over (content height of the pages past the limit) or to spare; the funder's rules from `PaperGrantRules.check` (problems listed, passes folded); wrapped figures wrapfig could not set beside text (`state.wrapReport`: `collision`, `end`, `held` far from its citation) with what to do; **Page settings** (typeface from the PAPPG list with its minimum, text size, line pitch ≥ 12 pt, paragraph space, caption size, gap beside wrapped figures, tighten paragraphs) written to `paperExports.lookOverrides` (`_saveLookOverrides`); the length of each section in pages and lines.
- **Fit to N pages** (`_fitLadder`, `_fitToLimit`): a ladder of compliant steps, gentlest first — every paragraph TeX can set a line shorter, captions 9.5 → 9 pt, line pitch 12.4 → 12.2 → 12 pt, text size down to the face's minimum — binary-searched by laying the document out for each candidate; **Keep** saves the overrides, **Undo** restores. Measured on the GELS CAREER Project Description: 16 → 15 pages (tighten, captions 9 pt, pitch 12 pt), and the compiled PDF is 15 pages too.
- `look.body.looseness` (override `body.looseness`, −1/0): `\AddToHook{para/begin}{\ifnum\looseness=0 \looseness=-1\relax\fi}` in the preamble; the preview applies it to every paragraph TeX's hook reaches, unless the paragraph sets its own (V3.910).
- Toolbar page count reads **N / limit pages** (red over, green within) on a grant document.
- Paper Lab: `drive.mjs check … --fit 1 [--keep 1]`, `compiledoc … --doc "<label>"`, `preview … --doc <key>`.

### Changed
- `paper-typeset.js` `breakLines`: with `\looseness ≠ 0` a pass that misses the asked-for line count hands on to the next (tex.web §873); `chooseFinal` picks TeX's way (nearest without overshooting, §875) and returns `actualLooseness`; candidates are pruned per line number when line numbers matter (`\looseness`, a per-line shape), within `\adjdemerits` of that line's best.
- Under a look the old lines-per-inch control is hidden and ignored, in the preview and the export (the look's line pitch rules).
- The layout check no longer calls a paragraph loose just because TeX reached its last pass while honouring a `\looseness`.

## [V3.912] — 2026-10-25 — Grants: wrapped figures set exactly as wrapfig sets them

Plan: [CodeLog/ClaudesPlan/V3.911_nsf_grant_format.md](../ClaudesPlan/V3.911_nsf_grant_format.md).

### Added
- Document view paginator models wrapfig 3.6 (one-column looks; `WRAP_TEX` in `_packPages`): a wrapped figure waits for the next paragraph start; it is set there when `\WF@size` (depth + 1.5 \baselineskip + 2 \intextsep) fits the room left (`\pagegoal − \pagetotal`), beside ⌊(size + 1.1 \baselineskip) / \baselineskip⌋ − 1 lines of `\linewidth − width − \columnsep`; otherwise it waits (the floating R/L form), unless less than a line is left, when the page breaks. Headings are never a placement point (the look gives them a 1sp hanging indent). A figure still waiting when the next wrapped figure begins is set alone after a `\bigskip` (`\WFclear`, "Collision"), outlined in the preview; one no paragraph took goes to the end. Wrapped paragraphs and headings are set again with per-line widths and offsets at `\tolerance 9999` (`_setWrappedPara`, `_setWrappedHeading`); `PaperTypeset.layoutParagraph` takes `widths` / `offsets` (a `\parshape`).
- Figures under a grant look are placed from a zero-height `.pdv-wrap-anchor` (`.pdv-wrapfig-tex`), carrying wrapfig's size, line count and room for the Paper Lab (`data-wf-*`).

### Changed
- `look.rigid_headings` (NSF): `\section`…`\subsubsection` are LaTeX's `\@startsection` with fixed space and a 1sp indent instead of titlesec — measured with Tectonic, titlesec headings break wrapfig (narrow lines carried on with no figure); the preview typesets these headings with Knuth–Plass like body text.
- The export writes `\begin{wrapfigure}{R|L}{w}` (floating form) under a look.
- Captions under a spec look are spaced by the caption package's struts: first baseline `\abovecaptionskip + 0.7 × lead` below the artwork, last line 0.3 × lead deep (`.pdv-figcap` margin-top / padding-bottom) — confirmed on wrapfigure boxes (to 0.07 pt) and on ordinary floats (bioRxiv: 15.70 bp).
- Measured item heights under a look are exact (no whole-pixel ceiling per item, which lost the line TeX fits at the foot of a page); a heading keeps a whole chain of headings plus two lines with it (`\@nobreak`).
- Paper Lab `sync.py`: a one-column page with a wrapped figure is one column; smaller type beside the text reads after the body.

### Results (GELS CAREER Project Description, Paper Lab)
- Preview and compiled PDF: 16 / 16 pages, **16 of 16 page starts identical**, 87 % of line ends; with Fit, 15 / 15 pages.

## [V3.910] — 2026-10-25 — Paper builder: a layout check in the Document view (loose lines, widows, orphans, stray figures, lines to save)

Plan: [CodeLog/ClaudesPlan/V3.906_paper_typesetting_fidelity.md](../ClaudesPlan/V3.906_paper_typesetting_fidelity.md) (P5).

### Added
- **Check** button in the Document view toolbar (journal looks; count badge) → `.pdv-check-panel` (`_openCheckPanel` / `_renderCheckPanel` / `_closeCheckPanel`). It lists, with page numbers and **Show** (scroll + flash):
  - loose lines (badness > 500, the emergency pass, overfull);
  - orphans (a paragraph's first line alone at a column foot) and widows (its last line alone at the next column's head);
  - figures and tables set ≥ 2 pages after their first mention (a ref chip, or "Fig. 3" / "Table 2" in the text; "Supplementary Fig." ignored);
  - how full the last page is, with **Tighten N paragraphs** when a few lines run onto it and enough paragraphs can lose one;
  - paragraphs `\looseness=-1` would set a line shorter, and the paragraphs you adjusted (**Reset**).
- **Tighten / Loosen** write `attrs.looseness` (−1 / +1) on the paragraph block (`_writeFigAttrs`). The Document view passes it to the line breaker (`_lineBreakParams`, `p.dataset.looseness`), and the exporter writes `\looseness=±1\relax` before the paragraph (`paragraphToTex`), so the PDF makes the same change.
- `_buildLayoutReport(geom)` after each mount. It reads `state.tsReport` (per-paragraph `lines`, `ratios`, `overfull`, `pass`, `canTighten`, `looseness` from `_typesetParagraphs`) and the mounted sheets (split parts carry their block id).
- `PaperTypeset.layoutParagraph(el, {probeTighten})` → `canTighten` (a second Knuth–Plass run with `looseness: -1`).
- Paper Lab: `drive.mjs check <id> <out> [--tighten-last 1 | --tighten 1 | --reset 1]` (panel text → `check.json`, `check.png`).

### Tests
- `scripts/tests/paper-tex-escape.test.mjs` 18/18 (two new `\looseness` checks); `paper-typeset.test.mjs` 25/25.
- Lab: PLOS → 3 orphans, 2 paragraphs that can lose a line. Tighten wrote `looseness: -1`, the preview re-set the paragraph, and the compiled section carries `\looseness=-1\relax`; Reset removed it.
- `sw.js` CACHE_VERSION 888 → 889.

## [V3.909] — 2026-10-25 — Paper builder: PNAS and IEEE pages from their own classes; TeX's vertical spacing in the Document view; a journal labeler

Plan: [CodeLog/ClaudesPlan/V3.906_paper_typesetting_fidelity.md](../ClaudesPlan/V3.906_paper_typesetting_fidelity.md) (results, P2–P4).

### Added
- **Class looks** (`look.engine: 'class'`, `rm/js/paper-look.js` `applyToTemplate`). The journal's own class sets the page: the template keeps its preamble and skeleton. The look adds `\microtypesetup{protrusion=false}` (when microtype is loaded) and `\AtBeginDocument{\frenchspacing\pretolerance=100 \tolerance=800 \emergencystretch=…}`, and hides the `hide_heading_kinds` headings. A class look describes the class's page for the Document view and never writes its own type into the .tex (`paper-export-tex.js` skips `texSectionOpen` for it).
  - **PNAS** (`pnas-new.json` `look`): geometry from `pnas-new.cls` (odd-page margins on Letter), LM 9 pt text, Helvetica at the class's 0.95 scale, abstract + keywords in column 1, inline affiliations, the first-page fact box, run-in ACKNOWLEDGMENTS, sans 6/8 bibliography. Every size is the class's TeX pt converted to bp.
  - **IEEE** (`ieee.json` `look`): IEEEtran [journal] measured from a compile. Times 10/12 with IEEEtran's retuned word spaces (0.35 em, 0.23–0.50; bold 0.375 em), `\hyphenpenalty 750`, `\relpenalty 800`, `\binoppenalty 1000`, Roman/A./1) numbering, small-caps centred heads, indented first paragraphs, run-in "Abstract—" / "Index Terms—" in column 1, the authors' note at the foot of column 1, "Fig. 1." captions, citations as "[2], [3], [4]".
- **Look options the Document view now draws**: `font_scale` (a family loaded scaled), `glue` per family and `<family>-bold` (`stretch`, `shrink`, `space` as fractions/em; CSS `--pts-stretch` / `--pts-shrink` / `--pts-space`, read per space by the typesetter), `kerning: false`, `body.topskip`, `title.before`, `abstract.mode: 'column'`, `abstract.parbox`, `abstract.first_indent`, `abstract.label_italic` / `label_sep`, `keywords.label` / `label_italic` / `label_sep` / `indent` / `before` / `after` / `family`, `affiliations.inline`, `affiliations.where: 'colnote'` (+ `prefix`, `indent`, `note_skip`), `authors.corresponding: false`, `factbox {specials, col, …}`, `indent_after_heading`, `case: 'smallcaps'`, section styles with `family` and `runin_head {text, family, size, weight, gap}` + `before`, `bib.family`, `cite.style: 'ieee'`, and `linebreak.hyphenpenalty` / `exhyphenpenalty` / `relpenalty` / `binoppenalty`.
- **Latin Modern optical sizes** `rm/vendor/fonts/lmroman9-*`, `lmroman8-*`, `lmroman7-regular` (GUST licence, from the TeX bundle) and FONTS `lm9` / `lm8` / `lm7`. A class that loads `lmodern` sets 9 pt text in LMRoman9, which is wider than LMRoman10 scaled down.
- **Journal labeler** (`ResearchManagement/data/figure-training/`, untracked dev tool): `harness.html?set=journals` with 22 region types (title … backmatter); `make_journal_set.py` (33 papers); `propose_journal.py` (run-based gutter/columns, figures, captions, headings, abstract, affiliations, references, footnotes); `scripts/paper-lab/journal_style.py` turns labels into per-journal style profiles and draft looks.
- **Paper Lab**: `calibrate.py` measures a look from any PDF; `sync.py` scores body and caption lines apart (`caption_line_ends`) and finds the gutter from body-size text only; `drive.mjs` records each typeset line's zone (`body` / `cap` / `front` / `bib`).

### Changed
- **TeX's vertical rhythm in CSS** (`paper-look.js` `lineOff` / `texGap` / `topGap`). TeX puts baselines `skip + \baselineskip(next)` apart; CSS puts them `(lead − off) + margin + off` apart, where `off` comes from the face's hhea metrics (`asc` / `desc` / `ht` added to every FONTS entry). Front matter, headings and caption skips now convert TeX skips into CSS margins. A box at the page top sits at its glyph height. Keywords follow the abstract (their top margin replaces the abstract's closing skip) and span with it.
- **Column capacity = TeX's**: `PaperLook.geometry` measures `\textheight + \baselineskip − \topskip`, so a column holds `floor((textheight − topskip)/baselineskip) + 1` lines, as in TeX (IEEE: 58, was 57).
- **`\sloppy` where LaTeX is sloppy**: captions, float contents, the fact box and a boxed abstract (anything after `\@parboxrestore`) break with tolerance 9999 and 3 em emergency stretch (`_lineBreakParams`).
- **The typesetter also sets** the abstract, keywords, figure/table captions, fact box and author note (`TYPESET_INNER_SEL`), not just body paragraphs. Centred or ragged captions keep the browser's breaks.
- **Float columns** (`_packPages` `tryFloatColumn`, `nextCol`). LaTeX's `\@tryfcolumn` at every column start: column floats at the head of the queue that fill ≥ `\floatpagefraction` take the column, centred. Column `[p]` floats wait for one instead of a whole page. A column can be named for a float (`float.col`), and a float can carry its own gap (`float.gapPx`).
- natbib numeric citations read "(5, 6)" / "[5, 6]" in the Document view (space after the comma).

### Bug Fixes
- **PNAS exports had no abstract**: `pnas-new.json` `main_template` now calls `\abscontent` after `\maketitle` (the research-article style sets it in column 1 only when asked, as the official template does).
- **An empty keywords environment** is dropped from main.tex (IEEEtran printed a bare "Index Terms—").
- **A height-capped figure overflowed its page in the Document view** on first open: it was built before its image's aspect was known. `_measureItems` now starts the render again once the decoded size is cached (once; cached images never wait).

### Tests
- Paper Lab, preview vs compiled: PNAS 7/7 pages, figures on the same pages (float column + float page as in the PDF), body line ends 60 %. ## [V3.908] — 2026-10-25 — Paper builder: the Document view sets text the way TeX does

Plan: [CodeLog/ClaudesPlan/V3.906_paper_typesetting_fidelity.md](../ClaudesPlan/V3.906_paper_typesetting_fidelity.md) (P3).

### Added
- **`rm/js/paper-typeset.js`** (`window.PaperTypeset`): `setPatterns` / `hyphenate` (Liang, TeX's en-US patterns with lefthyphenmin 2 / righthyphenmin 3), `breakLines(items, widths, params)` (Knuth–Plass with TeX's passes: pretolerance without hyphens, tolerance with them, then emergency stretch; demerits, adjdemerits, double/final hyphen demerits, looseness, an overfull rescue), `layoutParagraph(el, {width, indent, leading, params, atomic})` (measures text with DOM Ranges in the real fonts, builds box/glue/penalty items incl. breakable inline math at relations and binary operators with TeX's math glue, and rebuilds the paragraph as `span.pts-ln` lines justified exactly; baselines of tall lines fixed), `splitMathSource`, `breakableMathText`.
- **`rm/vendor/hyphen/hyph-en-us.js`**: hyph-utf8's US English patterns + exceptions (notice kept).
- Document view (`paper-doc-view.js`): `_typesetParagraphs` + `_lineBreakParams` before measuring; `_splitTypeset` splits a typeset paragraph at a line; LaTeX's float model under a look (`[t]` to the top of the current column, `figure*` from the next page, strict float order, float-page-first with the look's fractions, float pages centred, `notBeforePage`); headings keep with the next lines; bibliography as per-entry items; float-only columns never forced.
- `scripts/paper-lab/sync.py` (line-end, page-start and per-paragraph line-count agreement), `density.py`.

### Changed
- Looks set `\pretolerance=100 \tolerance=800 \emergencystretch=1.5em` (article's two-column `\sloppy` made line breaks unpredictable); the preview uses the same.
- Superscripts, subscripts and superscript citations at TeX's 0.7 em; inline KaTeX at the text size.

### Tests
- Corpus: preview pages = compiled for Nat Commun (14), JACS (11), bioRxiv (13); line-end agreement 71–92 %; no in-column gaps the PDF lacks.
- `sw.js` CACHE_VERSION 886 → 887.

## [V3.906] — 2026-10-25 — Paper builder: Paper Lab (real papers as ground truth) + export correctness

Plan: [CodeLog/ClaudesPlan/V3.906_paper_typesetting_fidelity.md](../ClaudesPlan/V3.906_paper_typesetting_fidelity.md) (P1).

### Added
- **Paper Lab** (`scripts/paper-lab/`): the real paper builder on a fake in-memory Firebase (`fake-firebase.js`, `lab-hooks.js`) served by `serve.py` (local Tectonic compile at `/paper-lab/api/compile`; refuses a workspace inside the repo), driven headless by `drive.mjs` (import / preview / compile), measured by `compare.py` (ORIGINAL | COMPILED | PREVIEW + ink metrics) and `run.py`; `gt_extract.py` / `gt_crop.py` for corpus PDFs. The corpus (7 published papers rebuilt as bundles) lives in `../PaperLab-corpus/`, outside every repo.

### Bug Fixes
- **Prose was not escaped** in the .tex (`paper-export-tex.js` `escapeProseTex`): `%` cut the rest of a paragraph, `& # _` broke the compile.
- **Inline math was not protected** from the markdown passes (`_protectInlineMath`): two `$…^…$` spans in a paragraph paired their carets → compile error.
- **Characters disappeared from the PDF** (’ – é ń μ …): XeTeX with T1 fonts drops them. Prose, titles, labels, captions and the .bib now carry TeX's ASCII forms (`uniToTex`, `bibEscape`; pages `--`).
- PLOS "Option clash for package xcolor" (`\PassOptionsToPackage{table}{xcolor}` first); 7 templates printed "Lead Author"; text continuing after a display equation is not a new paragraph (`PaperLayout.blockJoin`); captions span the column unless `caption_fit: 'box'`; table cells/notes go through the paragraph renderer; an equation block without `display` is inline in the Document view too.

### Tests
- `scripts/tests/paper-tex-escape.test.mjs` (16 checks). Corpus compiles with zero errors and zero missing characters.
- `sw.js` CACHE_VERSION 884 → 885.

Moved, it is an ordinary box. While floating it has `.box.clip-float` (z-index 5, lifted shadow), dropped on the `pointerup` that moves it.

## [V3.902] — 2026-10-24 — RM and Scientia always load the newest version after a deploy

Plan: [CodeLog/ClaudesPlan/V3.902_rm_files_always_fresh.md](../ClaudesPlan/V3.902_rm_files_always_fresh.md). Found when V3.901 was live on the server but Alex's browser still opened V3.900's Scientia: the host sends no `Cache-Control`, so browsers reused their copies for ~10% of a file's age without asking, and the worker's "network-first" `fetch(request)` went through that cache.

### Bug Fixes
- **`rm/.htaccess`** (new): `Cache-Control: no-cache` on `html?|js|mjs|css|json|webmanifest` under `/rm/` (`<IfModule mod_headers.c>` + `<FilesMatch>`). Every page, script and stylesheet is checked on each use; an unchanged one is a 304 with no body. Rehearsed in a local Apache with `AllowOverride FileInfo` (the class `l/.htaccess` proves the host allows); live headers checked after upload.
- **`sw.js` `revalidating(request)`**: `networkFirst` fetches with `cache: 'no-cache'`. Navigations (RM pages, the Scientia iframe) are asked for again by URL (`credentials: 'same-origin'`, `redirect: 'manual'`), since a `navigate` Request can't be re-made with options in every browser. This reaches copies saved before the header existed. CACHE_VERSION 880 → 881.
- **`scripts/deploy.py`**:
  - `_verify_set(…, uploaded)` accepts the 403 Apache gives every `.ht*` file once it has just been uploaded. `l/.htaccess` had been re-uploaded and reported "not verified" on every deploy.
  - `scientia_build_if_stale` also watches `rm/js/page-layout.js` and `rm/js/page-regions.js` (copied into the app since V3.901).

### Tests
- Local reproduction, with files changed on the server between two loads. Old worker: page and script old. New worker: page new, script old (Chrome's memory cache never asked). With `no-cache` and either worker: both new.

### Added
- **Clip a figure** (`scientia/src/13zza-clip.js`, `CLIP`): pointing at a figure or table on any PDF page (the card, the maximised view, the paper beside the note) shows "＋ Figure 2"; a click makes Gabe's image panel (`FIG.create` 1×1) in the column right of the card (`CLIP.spot`), drawn again from the PDF (`CLIP.canvas`: one viewport offset to the region, ~1600 px, WebP), titled with the label, the paper's caption as its text (from the page's words; cut off the picture when it sits below the artwork), `clip { src, media, page, rect, label, file }` and "from <paper>, p. N" (`DocView.box` wrapped → `CLIP.show` scrolls the reader / maximised view / card to the page and outlines the region).
- **Clip mode**: a scissors button on every PDF bar (`PDFW.bar` wrapped): every figure and equation outlined; a drawn box asks **Picture / Equation** (`CLIP.ask`); Esc ends it (window capture, before the maximised view's Esc).
- **Equations the way RM's paper reader captures them**: "＋ Equation 3" (`PAGE_REGIONS.detect`, the number read from the "(3)" level with it; the box made taller for sub/superscripts) → the snip (`CLIP.snip`, ~1000 px JPEG) → `CLIP.read` → LaTeX in Gabe's equation editor (`MATH.editor`, the snip above it, never over what you typed) → **an equation component** (`EQ.create`) with the same `clip`. `CLIP.read` is set by the web layer (`rm/scientia/lab-mode.js` §16: the lab's `equationOcr`, probed on first use, the user's token — the call `rm/js/equation-capture.js` makes); the desktop types it.
- **Detection inside Scientia**: `CLIP.detect` builds the page's words as the offline extractor does (`CLIP.items`), the artwork through `PAGE_LAYOUT.collectGraphics` with pdf.js 3.11's `constructPath` bounds reordered (`CLIP.ops`: 3.x writes `[minX, maxX, minY, maxY]`), an ink probe from a small render (`CLIP.probe`), then `figureRegions` and `PAGE_REGIONS.detect`; per media + page, on first hover.
- **Connections that follow the page**: each clip is wired to its paper (`c:clipped from`); a paper's wires to its clips and quotes are faint except those from the page it shows, which are solid and drawn again above the cards (`CLIP.pageOf`, `CLIP.mark` after every `drawWires` and as a paper scrolls).
- **Read beside the note** (`scientia/src/13zzb-reader.js`, `RDOCK`): the book on a card's bar (or "◧ Beside" on the maximised view) docks Gabe's maximised reader — its highlight panel, colour menu and pen highlighter (`MXHL.open`) — as **half the window**: `#app` two columns, the header across both, the note live in the other half. Bar: page n / N with ‹ ›, zoom − / % / + (Ctrl/⌘ + scroll), scissors, Highlights (a drawer), ⇄ side, ⤢ full screen, Close. ← → page while the pointer is over it; Esc never closes it. It stays with its note (`_ls rdock:<docId>`): leaving closes it, coming back reopens it. The card shows "Reading beside the note" meanwhile; quotes made in it are revealed in the note, and a quote's "from …" scrolls the reader.
- `scripts/scientia_build.py`: `VENDOR_COPY` refreshes `scientia/vendor/page-layout.js` + `page-regions.js` from `rm/js/` before Gabe's `build.py`; `--check` fails on a stale copy.

- `CodeLog/features.json`: `scientia.pdf` (13zk, 13zz, 13zza, 13zzb, the vendor copies), related to `rm.paper-reader`, distinct from it, from `rm.figure-board` and from `scientia.reader`.

### Changed

## [V3.899] — 2026-10-24 — Scientia: share or collaborate on a lit review or a project with anyone in the lab

Plan: [CodeLog/ClaudesPlan/V3.899_scientia_share_collaborate.md](../ClaudesPlan/V3.899_scientia_share_collaborate.md). Hub function deployed first (health V3.899); no rules change (the new collection is function-only).

### Added
- **The relay between hubs** — `functions/scientia-share-core.js` (new): the grant `shareWith {uid: 'read'|'edit'}` on a review's `documents` row or a project's `projects` row; copies marked `sharedFrom {uid, name, role, share}`; `closure` (review: the note, `blockIds`, wires with both ends inside, `items` born in it, `media` any component names (`m_…`); project: + its row, themes, aims, terms and every note filed in it, never someone else's copy); `relayPush(env, uid, commits)` after every push — owner's records → `fanOut` to each member (their row read, pushed with `prev`/`base` so a change they made meanwhile merges); a collaborator's → `inbound` into the owner's hub as device `share:<uid>` (`prev` = the shadow, `base` = its `ownerSeq`; `protect` keeps `shareWith`, `share`, `projectId`, `themeId`, a review's `projectIds`), then the owner's result out to everyone; a reader's → `revert` to the shadow (timestamps-only changes ignored: `sameish` skips `AUTO_MAX`); a changed grant → `sharePass` (lease on the index; collaborators' missed changes in first, closure recomputed, copies made equal, out-of-share and lost-access copies deleted, index rewritten); `relayMedia` copies a file uploaded after its record; `syncShares` = the hourly safety pass. `MemoryShareEnv` runs it all on MemoryHubs.
- **Its Firestore half** — `functions/scientia-share.js` (new): `firestoreEnv` (hubs through `FirestoreHub`, the index `scientiaShares/{owner}__{d|p}__{id}` written with `mergeFields` so the lease survives, shadows `…/shadow/{uid}__{store}__{id}`, `arrayUnion` id growth, a 3 s per-instance cache of the share lists), `labMembers` (not guest / hidden / collaborator / alumni).
- **Hub** (`functions/scientia-hub.js`, `scientia-hub-core.js`): `FirestoreHub.push` / `resolve` keep `lastCommits` (MemoryHub too); the handler relays after `api/sync/push`, `api/sync/resolve`, `api/media`; `GET api/rm/members`; `quietSyncs` runs `shares` (every 10 min check, hourly per share; `api/rm/sync?only=shares` forces); `noteLink` skips copies (a shared note is listed in RM once, under its owner).
- **Web app** (`rm/scientia/lab-mode.js` §15): a people button at the top right of each lit-review card and each Portfolio project header (count badge when shared); its panel (in the page) lists lab members with **Share** / **Collaborate** (tap again to take away) and a search box, or for a copy says who shared it, what you can do and who else has it; `setGrant` writes `shareWith` and kicks `shares`. Copies: "From Alex" / "With Alex" chips, a *Shared with you* section in the tab, a *shared* Portfolio group (+ Note only when collaborating). A read-only copy renders in Gabe's read-only (time-travel) view with the current state (`DocView.fill` wrapped; dock and title line say "Shared … · read only"; only the zoom pill); a collaborator's head block edits title/topic, not filing. `SIS_LAB.version` V3.899; `sw.js` 878.

## [V3.894] — 2026-10-24 — Scientia (web): PDF cards draw on demand — a note with many PDFs stays smooth

Plan: [CodeLog/ClaudesPlan/V3.894_scientia_pdf_cards_on_demand.md](../ClaudesPlan/V3.894_scientia_pdf_cards_on_demand.md). Alex: "when there are too many pdf's on the canvas it seems to slow down and the site glitches and freaks out". Web build only (`rm/scientia/lab-mode.js` §14); `scientia/src` untouched — the same change is Gabe's to review for the desktop: PR #1 `scientia/pdf-on-demand` (https://github.com/McGheeLab/McGheeLabWebsite/pull/1; `PDFW.onDemand` there makes §14 stand down). Numbering: V3.895 (zoom Shift-fit) landed first from a parallel session.

### Changed
- **A PDF card draws only while it is on screen** (`lab-mode.js` §14, `PDFW.body` + `WIDGETS.pdf.body` replaced; maximised view and phone layout keep Gabe's `PDFW.body`, `pane.maxView`): a shared viewport `IntersectionObserver` (400 px margin) activates a card; its page slots are built from the stored page count (sized from page 1's aspect, `PD.aspect`) and draw when inside the card's own scroll window (per-card observer rooted on the stage, 200 px); off screen for 4 s (`PD.idleMs`) → pages released (canvas 0×0, `.textLayer` / `.q-marks` removed); at most 6 idle parsed PDFs kept (`trimDocs`, LRU by `PD.used`; `PDFW.words` pins its document while it reads).
- **Survives a canvas rebuild**: `DocView.fill` rebuilds every box on each `changed()` (any sync); `PDFW.body` now returns the same viewer when the block object and what it shows are unchanged (`sigOf`: media, view, page in one-page view, pages, w, h, read-only; keyed per pane), moving its toolbar back from the old box's header (Gabe's `SLIM.dock` moves `.pdf-bar` into `.bh-tools`) so the new box docks it again.
- **As sharp as the zoom needs**: resolution = zoom × `devicePixelRatio` in ¼ steps, 0.5–3 (`resOf`); `Paper.prototype.apply` wrapped (debounced 220 ms) to redraw visible pages when off by > 1.25× / < 0.5×; a redraw renders into a new canvas swapped in when done (no white flash); at most 2 pages render at once (`PD.q`, `pump`). Below zoom 0.33 a card shows its title and page count (`.pdf-ph` on `.pdfw.pdf-far`, sized to the stage — the class names Gabe's version uses too) and gives its pages back.
- **Fetches only what it draws**: `PDFW.load` adds pdf.js `disableAutoFetch` + `disableStream` (range requests; Storage answers 206 with `Content-Range` exposed).
- Quotes: a page's first draw adds `QUOTE.textLayer` (what Gabe's `PDFW.page` wrapper did), so highlights and selection work; `QUOTE.goto` into a PDF while zoomed out below 0.33 zooms to 0.8 on the card (his reveal only zooms when the card is off screen). `PDFW.stats()` (also `SIS_LAB.pdf.stats`) → cards / active / drawn / MB / docs / queued. `SIS_LAB.version` V3.894.

### Measured (the ERK review: 28 PDFs, 660 pages; local Scientia, Retina 2×; `scripts/litreview/render/pdfload.mjs`)
- Opening the note (overview, zoom 0.3): before 57 pages drawn (4 on screen), 383 MB of canvas, 3.2 s of main-thread long tasks → after 0 pages (titles), 0.1 s.
- A sync from another device: before all 660 page slots rebuilt, 57 pages redrawn, 0.4 s freeze → after every canvas kept, 0.07 s.
- Reading one paper at 100 %: 57 pages / 383 MB → 4 pages (all on screen) / 27 MB; at 50 %: 6 pages / 10 MB. PDF files fetched: 28 → 4.

### Tests
- PR #1 tested the same way: harness 192/192 on its branch (§14 stood down, `PDFW` drew), and the desktop build on `serve.py` with the real note (same numbers, same behaviours).
- Lab-mode harness 192/192 (+10, §18: on-screen only, scroll window only, resolution, a rebuild keeps the canvases and the toolbar, zoomed out → titles and pages released, back in → drawn, one page at a time, panned away → released, maximise unchanged; fixture `scripts/tests/fixtures/pdf-6pages.pdf`). In the real app: a quote's "from …" from the overview → zoom 0.8, page 6 drawn, its 3 highlight rects; One at a time 5/38 → › 6/38; maximise draws.

### Bug Fixes
- A first version of §14 reached the site mid-work through a parallel session's end-of-turn deploy (with V3.893/V3.895): it lost a PDF card's toolbar after a sync and left a quote jump from the overview on the title. Fixed here (the toolbar is moved back before reuse; the jump zooms in).

## [V3.895] — 2026-10-24 — Scientia: Shift-tap with the zoom hand fits a component or region, its edge lit while Shift is held

Plan: [CodeLog/ClaudesPlan/V3.895_scientia_zoom_shift_fit.md](../ClaudesPlan/V3.895_scientia_zoom_shift_fit.md). The code went out in
`443f4987` (a parallel session's end-of-turn autopush, labelled V3.893); this entry records it.

### Changed
- **The ✎ pill's zoom hand** (`rm/scientia/lab-mode.js` §11, `bindZoomHand`, web build only):
  - **Unchanged:** tap = zoom in ×1.5 at the point, Alt-tap (or the right button) = out, drag up or down = smooth zoom.
  - **Shift-tap now fits** (Shift used to be a second "out"). It fits the view to what is under the pointer: a region by its name tab or its margin, a component (`.box` in the paper's world), or the whole note on empty paper. The fit is `Paper.fitTarget(bb, 48, P.o.maxZ)` + `animateView`, so a small component fills the screen up to the paper's max zoom.
  - New helpers `zfitTarget(host, x, y)`, `zfitMark(el)`, `zfitHover()`, `zfit(host, x, y)` and `zfitKeys(e)`, the shared `ZOOM_SKIP` selector, and the state `ZF { host, x, y, shift, el, swallow }`.
- **The lit edge:** while Shift is held, `.lab-zfit` on the target draws a teal outline. Its width is `--lab-zw` = 2 px ÷ zoom, kept at 2 px on screen by the `Paper.prototype.apply` wrapper.
  - It follows host `pointermove` and window `keydown`/`keyup` of Shift/Alt, so pressing Shift with a still mouse lights it.
  - It clears on `pointerleave`, window `blur` and leaving the zoom hand (`paintPills`).
- **Alt** shows the zoom-out cursor (`.canvas-host.lab-hand-zoom.lab-zoom-out`).
- **The click after a zoom-hand tap is swallowed** (400 ms, capture on the host), so a tap on a component or a plate header only zooms.
- The zoom mode's caption: "Zoom — tap to zoom in, Alt-tap out, Shift-tap to fit a component or region, drag up or down".

### Tests
- `scripts/tests/v3869-scientia-lab-mode-harness.html` §15: 7 new checks.
  - Alt-tap zooms out.
  - Shift lights the component under the pointer; releasing and re-pressing Shift turns it off and on.
  - Shift-tap centres the component and fits it.
  - Shift over a region's margin lights the region, and Shift-tap fits it.
- 182/182 headless. Screenshots of both highlights checked by eye.

### Bug Fixes (same day, after Alex tried it: "zooming into the correct magnification but not the right location")
- **Shift-tap now puts the fitted thing on the screen.**
  - **The bug:** `zfit` used `Paper.fitTarget`, whose vertical position is `Math.max(pad, …)`. That clamp keeps a note's top on screen, which is right for "fit everything". For one component or region further down the note, it snapped the view back to the top, so the zoom was right and the place was wrong.
  - **The fix:** `zfit` now computes the view itself. The target is centred in the room the side pills, the tool row and the dock leave (`ZFIT_PAD { side: 72, top: 64, bottom: 84, split: 100 }`, exposed as `SIS_LAB.zfitPad`; sides 12 px under 640 px wide). The zoom is the largest that fits, between the paper's `minZ` and `maxZ`.
  - Empty paper still uses `fitAll` (the note's top stays on screen).
- **The harness hid it.** Its component and region sat at the top of the note, where the clamp does nothing.
  - The test now moves the component to (896, 1400) and points the view at it at 60 %.
  - `centred()` checks both directions against `zfitPad`; it checked only the horizontal before.
  - 192/192 headless (10 of those are the parallel V3.894 session's).
- The fix was committed and deployed in `0b89bd65` (the V3.894 session's end-of-turn autopush).

## [V3.893] — 2026-10-24 — The PE-bead assay as a Scientia project, with three interactive simulators, set-up diagrams, a literature review and the validation plan

Plan: [CodeLog/ClaudesPlan/V3.893_pe_bead_scientia_project.md](../ClaudesPlan/V3.893_pe_bead_scientia_project.md). No site code changed, nothing was added to `deploy/site.json`, and there is no `sw.js` bump. A parallel session's end-of-turn autopush committed the simulator half of this work (pages, diagrams, figures, `params.py`, the report) as `bc534219 V3.892 (cont.)`; the rest lands here. The production writes are listed under "Published".

### Added
- **`scripts/scientia-project/build-project.js`** (+ README): a project spec → one Scientia project → a hub. It is the sibling of `scripts/litreview/build-note.js` for whole projects.
  - **Records:** projects, themes, aims (milestone weights must sum to 1), documents with regions, blocks, items, wires and media.
  - **Item kinds:** text (`**b**`, `*i*`, `$math$`, `$$display$$`, `[[cite:key]]`, `[[note:key|words]]`, list and checkbox lines, an optional structure on the first line, recorded under the project), figure, html, eq, calc, protocol (registered in its own note), plate and noteref.
  - **Equation legends** are keyed through Scientia's own `TEX` (loaded from `scientia/src/13n-eq.js`).
  - **Layout:** a column layout from estimated or measured heights (`--heights`).
  - **Ids:** deterministic, so a re-run updates in place and stale records of the project are deleted. A repeated item key in a note is an error.
  - **Push:** `--local` (a desktop `serve.py`) and `--cloud <uid> [--commit]` (`FirestoreHub.mediaPut` + `push`; only changed records).
- **`Research/bead_confocal_scientia/`:**
  - **`project-spec.js`:** project `p_pebeadaxr0` "PE bead assay on the AX R confocal".
    - **Themes:** four (binding, image formation, measurement strategy, validation), each with an aim and weighted milestones.
    - **Notes:** 21 — overview; binding model; image model; simulation results; measurement strategy; two set-up notes; validation approach; and 13 experiment protocol notes.
    - **Contents:** 62 structures (claims, questions, decisions, a barrier), 33 wires (questions and predictions → the protocol that answers each; equations → calculators), 9 equation blocks, 3 calculators, 22 figures, 3 HTML simulators, the Exp 12 plate, and citation chips to the review's papers.
  - **`protocols-to-scientia.cjs` → `protocols.json`:** the 13 RM protocol imports turned into note content, with `[!var:]` values computed at the defaults the way `protocol-formulas.js` computes them.
  - Also `heights.json` (measured on a desktop render), `render-check.mjs`, `library.json` and the README.
- **`Research/bead_confocal_sim/interactive/` (first committed in `bc534219`):**
  - **The pages** (self-contained, via `build.py`: shared `src/kit.js`/`kit.css`, `/*INCLUDE:*/`, and refusal of network loads, colour emoji and scripts that fail `node --check`):
    - `pe-bead-confocal.html` (image, focus, optical section, photons and bleaching);
    - `pe-bead-binding.html`;
    - `pe-bead-strategy.html`.
  - **`src/confocal-engine.js`:** `optics.py` ported, with two additions: saturation solved point by point (h = I/(1 + k₀I)·D) and free PE excluded from the bead's volume.
  - **Checks:** `tools/check_confocal.py` (PSF, H, F within 0.2 %; rendered F and rim peak within 0.6 %) and `tools/check_binding.py` (the engine block that ships, within 0.05 % over seven cases).
  - **Tables:** `tools/ray_table.py` (the bead-optics factor c(z) by material and objective) and `tools/strategy/` (the strategy page's PSF and saturation tables).
- **`Research/bead_confocal_sim/diagrams/` → `figures/setup_*.png`:** five set-up figures (the assay, the optical section through a shell, the AX R light path with settings, the standard-curve plate with the staggered wash, and the validation map), rendered by `render.mjs`.
- **`Research/bead_confocal_sim/params.py`:** one file for every shared number (R-PE, detection, operating point, detector, binding reference case).
- **`Research/PE_bead_confocal_litreview.md`:** 27 papers, 60 located quotes, four lanes. It is built with `scripts/litreview` (data in `~/Documents/GitHub/LitReviews/pe-bead-confocal/`), and the note links to the project.

### Changed
- **The simulator at the revision-2 operating point** (report §C.3 items 1–3):
  - `optics.py` and `binding.py` read their defaults from `params.py`: 2 µW, τ = 2.7 ns, and the report's binding reference case;
  - `BeadAssay` gains `D_AD`;
  - every figure and table was regenerated, and `tables.py` reads the operating point.
- **The report:**
  - Appendix S was rewritten to the new numbers (LOD table now matches §B.4.5; saturation solved point by point: F 5 % sublinear at ≈5–6 µW at 20x; the Vorselen 2020 caveat on the ray trace);
  - §C.3 records what is done.
- **The 13 RM protocols:** `make_protocols.py` updated the Exp 05, 06, 07 and 09 numbers; all 13 were regenerated, and `validate.cjs` passes all 13.
- **`PE_bead_confocal_experiments.md`:** the same numbers.

### Published (2026-10-24, Alex's request)
- **Alex's Scientia hub** (`userData/{uid}/scientia/hub`), two pushes:
  - **The project:** 17 media files (14 PNG, 3 HTML) and 411 records, hub seq 807 → 1218, 0 conflicts. Read back afterwards: all 411 records are identical to the build checked in the local render, and the three HTML pages are served as `text/html` with no attachment header.
  - **The literature review** (`d_lr3186c1484a`, linked to `p_pebeadaxr0`): 16 PDFs and 349 records, seq → 1567.
- **The lab library** (run by Alex, after the auto-mode safety check refused it for this session): 26 new items (15 with PDFs), Vorselen 2020 reused, tag `litreview:pe-bead-confocal`; undo list `library-manifest.json` in the review's data folder. The ids match the citation keys exactly. The hub's library mirror was then refreshed (27 written, 301 rows), and all 27 cited papers resolve.

The cx/cy shift now depends on the fast-axis smear, and the rim peak agrees with the JS engine to 0.6 % (it was 10 % off). ## [V3.890] — 2026-10-24 — Research: PE bead confocal assay — binding model, shell image simulation, measurement strategy

Plan: [CodeLog/ClaudesPlan/V3.890_pe_bead_confocal_model.md](../ClaudesPlan/V3.890_pe_bead_confocal_model.md). Research deliverable only — no site code, nothing in `deploy/site.json`, no `sw.js` bump.

### Added
- **`Research/PE_bead_confocal_assay_model.md`** — deep-research report (15 sources, 104 claims, 3-lens adversarial verification, all agents on Opus 5.5): one-step sandwich binding model on 8 µm beads with the pre-complex route and both k_off values; image-formation model of a fluorescent spherical shell on the Nikon AX-R (10x/0.45, 20x/0.75) in a single pinhole-set plane; simulation results across pinhole, laser, gain, PE density, bleaching, pixels per bead, dwell, focal offset, field position, objective; measurement strategy and first experiments.
- **`Research/PE_bead_confocal_experiments.md`** — 13 characterization experiments for the real AX R (power at the sample, photon-transfer gain, flat field, PSF / plane response / axial scaling, single-bead z-series in four modes, sampling and field position, bleaching / dark state / saturation / dwell-vs-averaging / antifade, gain ladder, backgrounds and excluded volume, PE calibration and PE:IgG ratio, association / post-wash dissociation / delayed detection / detection-antibody clamp / settling / bead number, standard curve and hook, head-to-head mode validation), each stating the parameter it pins and the decision it makes; a one-day subset; the plate-map CSV columns.
- **`Research/bead_confocal_sim/`** — `binding.py` (`BeadAssay(k1, km1, k2, km2, k3, km3, k4, km4, S_T, R_um, n_beads, V_uL, D_A, D_D, transport)`: `incubate()`, `wash()`, `endpoint()`, `curve()`, `sad_eq_excessD()`, `apparent_KD()`, `damkohler()`), `optics.py` (`ConfocalPSF(obj, pinhole_AU)` tabulated Gaussian-beam × pinhole-acceptance PSF with on-axis and plane-integrated z widths and `Veff`; `render(BeadState, ScanSettings)` → image, photon map, metrics; `integrated_analytic()` hat-box check; `bleach_fraction_per_frame()`), `run_figures.py` (9 figures, `results.json`; per-figure CLI), `tables.py`, `README.md`.

## [V3.887] — 2026-10-23 — Speech to text, each person's own way: free on the device, or their own OpenAI / Google key; Transcribe in Scientia and in the board replay

Plan: [CodeLog/ClaudesPlan/V3.887_speech_to_text_your_own_way.md](../ClaudesPlan/V3.887_speech_to_text_your_own_way.md) — recorder R3, rewritten by Alex the same day: no lab-paid service; each person chooses and sets up their own way in Settings; still on a button that shows the likely cost first. No backend, rules or Storage change.

### Added
- **`rm/js/speech-to-text.js`** (`window.STT`): `settings() / save(patch)` (in `localStorage` `rm:stt:<uid>` — this browser, this sign-in; never Firebase), `ready()` → `{ ok, provider, why: 'none' | 'key' }`, `estimate(sec, provider)`, `transcribe(blob, { ext, onProgress, signal })` → `{ segs: [{ s, e, text }], lang, provider, model }`, `check(provider, key)`, `mountSettings(el)`. Engines: **device** (Whisper `onnx-community/whisper-base.en` q8 via transformers.js 3.8.1 in a module worker, 5-minute pieces), **openai** (`whisper-1`, `verbose_json` + segment timestamps; the file as-is ≤ 24 MB, else 10-minute 16 kHz WAV pieces), **google** (V1 `speech:recognize?key=`, 55-second LINEAR16 pieces four at a time, `latest_long`, word times → a sentence a line). `decode16k` (OfflineAudioContext at 16 kHz, channels mixed), `wav`, `sentences`. Errors in plain words (refused key, no credit, API off, billing off, key restricted to other sites).
- **`rm/js/stt-device-worker.js`**: the module worker (`{type:'load'}`, `{type:'run', pcm}` → chunks with times; download progress posted).
- **Settings → Speech to text** (`rm/js/settings.js` tab `speech`; `?tab=speech` / `#speech` open a tab directly; `rm/pages/settings.html` loads `recorder-core.js` + `speech-to-text.js`; `.stt-*` in `rm/css/settings.css`): On this device (free, *Download it to this device now*), OpenAI Whisper, Google Speech-to-Text, Off; a minute's and an hour's cost for each; key field (hidden, Show, **Check the key**, Forget it) and the step-by-step setup for each (5 for OpenAI, 6 for Google incl. restricting the key to the API and `https://mcgheelab.com/*`).
- **Scientia (web)**: a recording saved in the lab's cloud shows **Transcribe — about 18¢** / **Transcribe on this device — free** / **Set up speech to text ↗** (`lab-mode.js` `sttEl`, `transcribeRec`, `recBlob`; progress + Stop in the card); the lines go through Gabe's `REC.apply` like his desktop's; `rec.stt = { provider, model, at }`. `speech-to-text.js` is loaded with the lab layer. `SIS_LAB.version` V3.887.
- **Board replay** (`whiteboard-replay.js`): the owner's **Transcribe** under the replay bar (`ensureStt`, `renderWords`, `transcribeRec`; the joined audio `R.blob`); the lines are kept on the recording doc as `transcript { segs, provider, model, lang, at }`; a transcript panel (Hide / Show) where a tap plays from that line and the line being spoken lights up (`paintLine` via `lineAt`). CSS `.wb-rp-words / .wb-rp-line / .wb-rp-pbar` in `whiteboard-board.css`.

### Changed
- `recorder-core.js`: `STT_USD_PER_MIN` → `STT_RATES { device: 0, openai: 0.006, google: 0.024 }` (checked 2026-10-23); `sttCost(sec, provider | rate)`; a zero rate reads "free".

### Tests

Next, we stain the cells and image them on the confocal." — in 13 s including the model download).
