New `else if (ref)` branch in the `_renderPanel` actions block fires when a ref is parsed but has neither DOI nor arXiv id, rendering a `<a class="btn btn-sm lp-cite-lookup" target="_blank">Look up</a>` pointing at the Scholar URL. Existing `+ Add to library` / `+ Add (arXiv)` / `Open paper →` actions for refs with identifiers are unchanged. The `no id` chip is kept alongside the new button — it still explains why auto-add isn't available.

### Changed
- **`sw.js`** — `CACHE_VERSION` 79 → 80.

### Notes
- The user's loop is: click Look up → verify on Scholar → grab the DOI from Scholar's record → come back and add via the existing DOI flow. A future enhancement could close that loop (Look up → "I found it, here's the DOI" → fire `+ Add to library` directly), but Scholar blocks easy automated DOI extraction so it's left as a manual step for now.
- **Hard-reload required** to evict SW cache `mcgheelab-shell-v80`.

## [V3.104] - 2026-05-08

**Paper builder: skeleton becomes a real bullet outline + per-bullet claim flag.** Second of four planned wishlist features (`rm/wishlist.md` "paper builder"). Ships two coupled changes: the skeleton field is promoted from a flat `Y.Text` to a `Y.Array<Y.Map>` outline (with depth/indent and per-bullet metadata), and each bullet can now be **optionally** flagged as a claim — flagged bullets carry a `claim_id` pointing at the existing `drafts/{paperId}/claims/{claimId}` Firestore docs and surface a status pill that tracks lit-review progress. Most bullets stay unflagged plain outline. Plan: [CodeLog/ClaudesPlan/V3.104_skeleton_claims.md](../ClaudesPlan/V3.104_skeleton_claims.md).

### Added
- **`rm/js/paper-schemas.js`** — `MAX_SKELETON_DEPTH = 3` constant and `newSkeletonItem({text, depth, claim_id})` factory exposed on `window.PaperSchemas`. `newParagraph()` now seeds `skeleton_items: [newSkeletonItem()]` (one empty depth-0 bullet) alongside the legacy `skeleton: ''` field — keeping both means a one-version rollback to V3.102 still has a flat field to render from.
- **`rm/js/paper-blocks.js`** — `migrateSkeletonToItems(yBlock, Y)`: idempotent first-render migration. If `skeleton_items` is absent or empty, parse the legacy `skeleton` Y.Text (split on `\n`, leading-spaces ÷ 2 → depth, capped at `MAX_SKELETON_DEPTH`, leading `- ` stripped) and seed `skeleton_items` in a single Yjs transaction. Race-safe via length-check inside the transact callback. Legacy `skeleton` field is preserved.
- **`rm/js/paper-blocks.js`** — `renderSkeletonOutline(yBlock, ctx)` replaces the old flat `skEl` contenteditable in `renderParagraph`. Mounts a flex-row outline (depth → inline `padding-left = depth*22px`); each `<div.pe-skeleton-item>` carries a marker, a `<div.pe-skeleton-bullet>` contenteditable bound via the existing `bindYTextToContentEditable` (so `$math$` and `[@cite]` tokens work inside bullets), a hover-only `⚑` flag-as-claim button (visible only when `claim_id` is null), and a `<button.pe-claim-pill>` status pill (visible only when `claim_id` is set). Per-bullet keydown handler implements: `Tab`/`Shift+Tab` indent/outdent (writes `depth` via Yjs transact), `Enter` splits the bullet at caret (left half stays in-place, right half goes into a new Y.Map at index+1 with same depth, focus moves to the new bullet via a `pendingFocusId` resolved after the array-observer-driven re-render), `Backspace` at start of empty bullet deletes the item (focus moves to prior), `Backspace` at start of non-empty bullet merges into the prior bullet at the same depth. `Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+L` opens the flag-as-claim modal for the focused bullet (or the detail panel if it's already flagged). The outline always keeps at least one bullet — deleting the last one auto-seeds an empty one.
- **`rm/js/paper-bullet-claims.js`** (new) — slim bridge between bullets and the existing `window.CLAIMS` namespace from `rm/js/claims.js`. `attach(paperId)` opens a single `CLAIMS.subscribe(paperId, ...)` subscription per editor mount, caches `claimId → claim doc` in module state, and dispatches a `paper-claims-changed` window event so all rendered pills can refresh. `getClaim(claimId)` is the synchronous lookup for pills. `flagBullet({yBlock, itemMap, paperId})` opens a small modal (statement prefilled from bullet text + initial-status select), calls `CLAIMS.create(paperId, {statement, status})`, then writes the returned `claim_id` back into the bullet Y.Map in a Yjs transaction. `openClaimDetail(claimId)` mounts a slide-out panel listing the claim's `supporting_evidence_ids` / `counter_evidence_ids` with deep links to `/rm/pages/library-paper.html?id=<paperId>#ann-<annId>` and a status changer that calls `CLAIMS.update`. No new Firestore paths or rules — the existing `drafts/{draftId}/claims/{claimId}` rule (firestore.rules:600-607) already permits the claim CRUD.
- **`rm/css/paper-editor.css`** — `.pe-skeleton-outline` (overrides `.pe-block-content` `pre-wrap` to `normal` so the flex layout works), `.pe-skeleton-item` (flex row), `.pe-skeleton-marker`, `.pe-skeleton-bullet` (italic, focus glow), `.pe-skeleton-flag-btn` (opacity 0 → 1 on row hover or focus), `.pe-claim-pill[data-status=…]` (developing=amber, needs-more-evidence=red, supported=green, abandoned=struck-through gray, loading/unknown=neutral). Modal styles `.pe-claim-flag-modal-*` (overlay + 520px card + statement textarea + status select + cancel/save). Slide-out panel `.pe-claim-detail-panel` (right-anchored 360px, supporting/counter evidence sections with stance-tinted headings, deep-link evidence pills, status changer).

### Changed
- **`rm/js/paper-blocks.js`** — `renderParagraph` now calls `migrateSkeletonToItems(yBlock, Y)` then mounts `renderSkeletonOutline` instead of the old flat-skeleton `bindYTextToContentEditable`. Skeleton/body view-mode toggle and skeleton/body filter still work — they just toggle the outline container's `display` rather than a single contenteditable.
- **`rm/js/paper-export-tex.js`** — `paperTreeFromYDoc` now also extracts `skeleton_items` as a structured array of `{id, depth, text, claim_id}` per block. New helper `prefixSkeletonComment(block)` emits the bullets as a `% Skeleton:` LaTeX comment block above the body, indented per depth (`%   - top`, `%     - sub`). Falls back to the legacy flat `skeleton` text for blocks that haven't been migrated yet. `paragraphToTex` prepends the comment; `figureToTex` does not (figures don't have outline structure). Skeleton is authoring scaffold, not publication content, so comments preserve it for the human writer without affecting the rendered manuscript.
- **`rm/pages/paper-builder.html`** — editor-mode script list now also loads `claims.js` (existing) and `paper-bullet-claims.js` (new) before `paper-blocks.js`, so the renderer can probe `window.CLAIMS` and `window.PaperBulletClaims` when binding the bullet ⚑ button.
- **`rm/js/paper-editor.js`** — `connectAndRender` now calls `window.PaperBulletClaims.attach(state.paperId)` right after the Yjs connect resolves, so the per-paper claims subscription is live by the time the first paragraph block renders. Tolerates a missing `PaperBulletClaims` (script load order in standalone tests) — pills then sit in their loading state, harmless.
- **`sw.js`** — `CACHE_VERSION` 78 → 79.

### Reused infrastructure (no edits)
- **`rm/js/claims.js`** — full `subscribe` / `create` / `update` / `remove` / `addEvidence` / `removeEvidence` CRUD against `drafts/{draftId}/claims/{claimId}`. `addEvidence`/`removeEvidence` already runs both sides of the link (annotation `evidence_for_claim_ids` ↔ claim `supporting_evidence_ids`/`counter_evidence_ids`) atomically in a single transaction.
- **`firestore.rules`** lines 595-607 — already permits any `isLabContributor()` to create / edit / delete claim docs at `drafts/{draftId}/claims/{claimId}`. No rules edit required.
- **`rm/js/annotation-panel.js`** lines 335-380 — already has the "Tag as evidence" form with a draft + claim picker that calls `CLAIMS.addEvidence(draftId, claimId, paperId, annId, stance)`. The writer's flagged bullets simply appear in the existing claim picker once the user enters the paper's draftId on the reader side. No edits required.

### Notes
- **The skeleton schema migration is idempotent.** First time a paragraph block renders post-V3.104, the legacy `skeleton: Y.Text` is parsed and `skeleton_items: Y.Array` is populated. Subsequent renders no-op (skip-on-non-empty length check). Two clients racing the migration is safe — both write inside `yDoc.transact`, the second client's check finds non-empty items and bails. Legacy `skeleton` is *not* deleted; rolling back to V3.102 still has a field to read from.
- **Most bullets stay unflagged.** Claim flagging is opt-in via the `⚑` button or `Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+L`. Bullets that are notes, methodological details, or author introspection should not be flagged. Unflagged bullets carry no Firestore doc, no pill, no lit-review hookup.
- **Drag-reorder is decorative for V3.104.** The bullet has no drag handle in this version (paragraph-level reorder lands in a later wishlist item). Reorder via Backspace-merge / Enter-split / Tab-indent gives reasonable structural control without it.
- **Body rich text is V3.105.** The bullet text uses the existing paragraph render contract — `$math$` and `[@cite]` work today, but markdown tokens (`**bold**`, `*italic*`, `~sub~`, `^sup^`, `` `code` ``) ship in the next wishlist item.
- **The "draftId" arg in `CLAIMS.*` is the paper's `id` slug.** No bridging required — the paper-builder paper IS conceptually the draft. The Firestore path `drafts/{paperId}/claims/{claimId}` works as-is.
- **Hard-reload required** to evict SW cache `mcgheelab-shell-v78` and pick up `paper-bullet-claims.js` + `claims.js` on the editor.
- **No deploy step** beyond the static FTP push — Firestore rules / indexes are unchanged from V3.103.

## [V3.103] - 2026-05-08

**Drafts replace project buckets in the paper-reader linkage model.** Reported: "In the project folder, there are papers that we are writing, and there are grants that we are writing. these are what we want to attach to papers so that we can easily add these papers as references to the paper or grant that we are drafting. The add evidence button should select from only the list of paper drafts or grant drafts that are associated with the paper. we can add a paper draft or grant draft from the evidence page as well."

The V3.94–V3.98 picker linked library papers to *project buckets* (`tasks/buckets.json`) — the wrong scoping unit. The lab's actual workflow is: associate a library paper with the paper drafts and grant proposals it's evidence for, then per-annotation tagging picks among those associated drafts. V3.103 swaps the paper reader from buckets to drafts wholesale.

### New schema field
- **`items.json` library paper:** `meta.library.linked_drafts: [draft-id]` — paper drafts (paper-builder, items.json `type: 'paper'` AND NOT `is_library_entry`) and grant proposals (items.json `type: 'grant'` with status in `drafting | submitted | under_review | revising | rejected`) this library paper is evidence for. Empty / missing = "not linked to any draft yet" (no per-paper shortlist; the inline "+ Link draft…" affordance creates one).

### Changed
- **`rm/js/paper-overlays.js`** — refactored from `bucket_ids` / `linked_bucket_ids` / `tasks/buckets.json` to `cite_in_drafts` / `meta.library.linked_drafts`. Public API exposes `getActiveDraftIds`, `getLinkedDrafts`, `getColorForDraft`, `linkDraft`, `unlinkDraft`, `openLinkPicker`. Backward-compat aliases (`getActiveBucketIds`, `getLinkedBuckets`, `getColorForBucket`) operate on drafts now to keep one-cycle compat with downstream call sites. Active-set localStorage key bumped from `rm_lp_overlays_<paperId>` to `rm_lp_drafts_<paperId>` so old bucket-active sets don't leak into the draft system. Filter function checks `cite_in_drafts` (with `bucket_ids` fallback only inside annotation-overlay.js stripe rendering, for legacy data).
- **`rm/js/paper-overlays.js`** — "+ Link to project bucket…" button + modal becomes "+ Link to draft…". Two sections (**Paper drafts** / **Grant drafts**) populated from `items.json`. Each row shows a per-draft swatch + title + `(funder · mechanism · status)` hint. Save writes the new `meta.library.linked_drafts` array directly (single API call). Search input filters live across sections. The free-form "+ Create + link" inline form retired — drafts are entities created on the projects pages, not from the reader.
- **`rm/js/annotation-overlay.js`** — left-edge stripe rendering driven by `cite_in_drafts` (falls back to `bucket_ids` for legacy annotations) and `getActiveDraftIds()` / `getColorForDraft()`.
- **`rm/js/annotation-panel.js`** — "Drafts" row in the per-annotation card now lists per-paper-linked drafts only. Inline `+ Link draft…` button calls `PAPER_OVERLAYS.openLinkPicker()` so the user can extend the shortlist without leaving the card. Empty-state copy switches from "none" to "no drafts linked yet" when the paper has no `meta.library.linked_drafts`. The redundant "Overlays" bucket-chip row in `_renderInfoPanel` is retired (drafts now do all the scoping).
- **`rm/js/library-paper.js`** — `_drafts` filter (a) accepts `type: 'grant'` items in proposal-status as well as paper drafts, and (b) is filtered to `meta.library.linked_drafts` for this paper before passing to the annotation panel. New `_allDrafts` holds the full pool (used implicitly by the link picker; `_drafts` is the per-paper shortlist). `PAPER_OVERLAYS.onChange` callback now reloads `items.json` and re-derives `_drafts` so the panel's selectors update immediately after the user adds / removes a linked draft.
- **`rm/js/paper-overlay-import.js`** — frontmatter accepts `draft_id` (preferred) or legacy `bucket_id`. Validation surfaces `draftOk` / `draftTitle` / `draftId` (with `bucket*` aliases for the existing preview-modal copy). Imported highlights' `cite_in_drafts` is the union of any per-highlight `cite_in_drafts: [...]` plus the file-level draft id. Auto-link on import calls `PAPER_OVERLAYS.linkDraft` (writes `meta.library.linked_drafts`) instead of `LINKS.addLink` (which wrote `linked_bucket_ids`). Idempotency check now matches on `(quote, page, draft)` instead of `(quote, page, bucket)`.
- **`rm/css/style.css`** — `.lp-overlay-kind` paper / grant chip on overlay popover rows; `.ann-draft-link` button (purple accent) for the inline "+ Link draft…" affordance.
- **`sw.js`** — `CACHE_VERSION` 77 → 78.

### Notes
- **Pre-V3.103 `bucket_ids` data on annotations is preserved** but no longer drives the overlay filter. annotation-overlay.js's stripe rendering falls back to `bucket_ids` when `cite_in_drafts` is empty so existing data still renders coherently. New annotations only get `cite_in_drafts`.
- **The `tasks/buckets.json` system itself is untouched.** The dashboard, projects page, and tasks tab still use it; we just removed its surface in the paper reader. `LINKS.addLink` etc. continue to operate on `linked_bucket_ids` — independent from the new `meta.library.linked_drafts`.
- **`evidence-tag-dialog.js` is untouched** because nothing imports it; the inline evidence form in `annotation-panel.js` is the active path. It can be deleted in a follow-up.
- **`.paper-overlay.md` files written by the `/paper-overlay` skill** with `bucket_id:` keep working (legacy fallback). Update the skill at `.claude/skills/paper-overlay/SKILL.md` to use `draft_id:` going forward (not done in this change; left as a one-line edit).
- **Hard-reload required** to evict SW cache `mcgheelab-shell-v78`.

## [V3.102] - 2026-05-08

**Paper builder: editable figure block (image upload + LaTeX render options).** First of four planned wishlist features (`rm/wishlist.md` "paper builder" — figures, skeleton outlining + claims, body rich text, equation refs). The figure block kind has lived in the schema since Phase A (`PAPER_BLOCK_KINDS` in `rm/js/paper-schemas.js`) but rendered "(unsupported in this phase)". This wires it up end-to-end: drop an image into the editor, tune `\includegraphics` options inline, and have it round-trip through Yjs and the LaTeX export. Plan: [CodeLog/ClaudesPlan/V3.102_figures.md](../ClaudesPlan/V3.102_figures.md).

### Added
- **`rm/js/paper-figures.js`** (new) — Firebase Cloud Storage upload helper for figures. `uploadImage(paperId, blob)` SHA-256s the blob, checks `getMetadata()` first to skip re-billed re-uploads, writes to `paper-figures/{paperId}/{shortHash}.{ext}` with a custom-metadata stamp (`uploadedBy`, `fullHash`, `paperId`), and resolves `getDownloadURL()`. Allowlist: PNG/JPG/GIF/WebP/SVG/PDF, 15 MB cap. Returns `{storage_path, hash, full_hash, mime, size_bytes, uploaded_at, uploaded_by, download_url, already_existed}`. Path prefix is intentionally distinct from `papers/{paperId}/` (the PDF library) so the storage rule there can stay PDF-only.
- **`rm/js/paper-blocks.js`** — `renderFigure(yBlock, ctx)` replaces the old `renderUnsupported('Figure')` dispatch. Toolbar matches the equation-block shape (handle, kind tag, status pill, delete). Below it: image preview frame; upload row (`<input type=file>` proxied through a button + status text); collapsible "Layout" details with width (text input + datalist of common LaTeX widths), placement (`H`/`h`/`t`/`b`/`p` select), centering checkbox, label (auto-prefixed with `fig:`, slugified), alt text; caption pane bound to the block's `body` Y.Text via `bindYTextToContentEditable` so cite/math tokens render the same way they do in paragraphs. Imported figures with legacy `attrs.raw_tex` surface the LaTeX source in a read-only `<details>` so the user can rebuild from it. All attrs writes go through `yDoc.transact` with named origins (`figure-upload`, `fig-width`, `fig-placement`, `fig-center`, `fig-label`, `fig-alt`); the attrs observer reflects remote edits into form fields, skipping any input the local user is currently focused on so in-flight typing isn't clobbered.
- **`rm/js/paper-editor.js`** — `addFigure(secId)` mirrors `addEquation` shape but seeds the V3.102 figure attrs (`storage_path`/`download_url`/`hash`/`mime` empty, `width: '\linewidth'`, `placement: 'H'`, `centering: true`, empty `label`/`alt`). The `+ Figure` button is appended to `pe-add-block-row` after `+ Equation`, gated on `PaperSchemas.styleFor(section).allowFigures` — abstract / keywords / conclusions / acknowledgements / references suppress it; everything else allows it. Render-block ctx now also carries `paperId` so the figure renderer can build the Storage path.
- **`rm/js/paper-schemas.js`** — `newFigure()` factory + `PaperSchemas.newFigure` export. Used by paper-editor's `addFigure` and exposed for any future tree-builders.
- **`rm/css/paper-editor.css`** — `.pe-block-figure` styles: `.pe-figure-preview` (dashed-border placeholder, `display:flex` for centered empty hint or `<img>`); `.pe-figure-img` (max-height 480px, max-width 100%, soft shadow); `.pe-figure-uploadrow` (button + status text); `.pe-figure-layout` (collapsible `<details>`, two-column grid of fields); `.pe-figure-caption` (rounded-border content area on focus); `.pe-figure-rawtex` (legacy import preview). Field labels are uppercase 11px gray to match the broader editor chrome.

### Changed
- **`rm/js/paper-export-tex.js`** — `figureToTex` rewritten to read the V3.102 attrs schema first, falling back to legacy `attrs.path` and ultimately `figures/PLACEHOLDER.pdf`. Source path derived from `attrs.storage_path` as `figures/<basename>` (the export server is expected to mirror the Storage blob into `<repo>/figures/`). `centering` becomes conditional on `attrs.centering` (default true). `label` defaults to `attrs.label` when set, else `fig:<block.id>`. Caption is read from `block.body` (the Y.Text the figure block now binds) and run through `paragraphTextToTex` so `[@cite]` and `**bold**` tokens emit the same LaTeX they do in paragraph bodies; legacy imports with `attrs.caption` still work. `collectCitationKeys` now scans figure captions in addition to paragraphs, so a `[@key]` cited only inside a caption still ends up in the bib.
- **`rm/pages/paper-builder.html`** — load `firebase-storage-compat.js` (10.14.0 CDN) alongside the existing app/auth/firestore SDKs (figure upload uses `firebase.storage()`); add `/rm/js/paper-figures.js` to the editor-mode script list before `paper-blocks.js`.
- **`storage.rules`** — new `paper-figures/{paperId}/{=**}` matcher: authenticated read for any signed-in user; authenticated write up to 15 MB, content-type must match `image/.*` or be `application/pdf`. Sits next to (not inside) the existing `papers/{paperId}/` PDF-only matcher so neither rule loosens the other. Deploy: `firebase deploy --only storage:rules`.
- **`sw.js`** — `CACHE_VERSION` 76 → 77.

### Notes
- **Hard-reload required** to evict SW cache `mcgheelab-shell-v76` and pick up `paper-figures.js` + `firebase-storage-compat.js`.
- **Storage rules deploy is required** before figure upload works in production. Run `firebase deploy --only storage:rules` from the parent repo root after merging.
- **Caption is the figure's body, not a separate attr.** This intentionally repurposes the block's existing `body` Y.Text field so the existing `bindYTextToContentEditable` binding works unchanged and the export pipeline runs the caption through the same `paragraphTextToTex` cite/math expansion. Legacy imports with `attrs.caption` are still read by `figureToTex` so old papers don't lose their captions.
- **Width datalist is suggestions, not validation.** The user can type any LaTeX width spec (e.g. `0.7\linewidth`, `5cm`, `\textwidth - 2cm`); the value is emitted verbatim into `\includegraphics[width=…]`. The datalist just provides single-click presets for the common values.
- **Label is auto-prefixed with `fig:`.** When the user types a bare slug (e.g. `cellgrowth`), blur normalizes to `fig:cellgrowth` (kebab-cased, lowercased, alphanumeric+`_-`). Already-prefixed values pass through. This keeps `\eqref`/`\ref` resolution consistent with the equation-block's `eq:`-prefix convention.
- **Where the LaTeX export expects to find the image.** `figureToTex` emits `\includegraphics{figures/<basename>}` where `<basename>` is the last segment of `storage_path` (`<sha256-short>.<ext>`). The actual file mirroring from Storage into `<repo>/figures/` is left to the export server (`/api/paper/export-tex`) — extending that endpoint to fetch `download_url` and write it under `figures/` is the next step before the LaTeX export compiles end-to-end.
- **Drag-reorder of figures is not implemented yet.** The handle (`⋮⋮`) is decorative on this block kind, matching the equation/paragraph state. Block reorder lands in a later wishlist item.

## [V3.101] - 2026-05-08

**Citations panel: per-digit reverse hover + pixel-perfect highlight rects.** Reported: "when we hover over a citation link on the page, the citations are not individually selectable with hover ... Also the highlights are not in the correct spot, they are slightly off but are better overlaid when the citation is closer to the left side of the page." Two leftover issues from V3.99/V3.100 — both rooted in how rects were derived and how hover listeners were bound.

### Bug Fixes
- **`rm/js/paper-citations.js`** — reverse hover (PDF → panel) didn't separate cluster digits. `_wirePageTokenHover` bound `mouseenter` listeners to each pdf.js text-layer *span* with a `__citeHoverBound` flag; when a cluster like `[1,2,3]` lived in one span (the common case), the first match won the binding and refs 2 and 3 were silently skipped. Rewritten to render one transparent `.pv-cite-hit` div per match into the existing `pv-cite-overlay` layer with `pointer-events: auto` — so ref 1, ref 2, ref 3 each get their own hover region. Re-binding clears prior `.pv-cite-hit` children so page nav / re-renders don't leak listeners.
- **`rm/js/paper-citations.js`** — flash rects were drifting off the digit, worse near the right side of the page. V3.99's `_rectForRange` used a char-fraction approximation (`localStart / itemLen * item.width`) that assumes uniform glyph width — wrong for proportional fonts + kerning, with error growing with x-offset (matching the reported "better on the left side" symptom). Replaced with a DOM `Range` based path: `_rectForRangeViaDom` builds `range.setStart(span.firstChild, localStart)` / `.setEnd(...)` against each text-item's underlying text-layer span (`item.domSpan`, already exposed by `pdf-viewer.js`'s `_collectTextItems`), reads `range.getClientRects()` for pixel-perfect rendered rects, and subtracts the page wrap's viewport rect to get wrap-local coords. The V3.99 char-fraction math is kept as `_rectForRangeViaFraction` and used as a fallback when `domSpan` isn't available. `_scanPage` now captures the page wrap's `getBoundingClientRect()` once and threads it through every match.

### Changed
- **`sw.js`** — `CACHE_VERSION` 75 → 76.

### Notes
- **Side effect:** native text selection over a citation marker (the digits inside `[1,2,3]`) is now blocked — `pointer-events: auto` on the hit-rect captures clicks/drags. Selection on the surrounding sentence is unaffected (the hit-rects are tight to the match). Acceptable trade-off for fixing the per-digit hover, since selecting citation glyphs specifically is rare.
- **Hard-reload required** to evict SW cache `mcgheelab-shell-v76`.

## [V3.99] - 2026-05-08

**Citations panel: cluster citations expand into one row per ref + flash highlights only the marker.** Reported: "on the citations on page viewer, when there is a cluster of citations e.g. [1,5,9] the citations are not separated and we only see the 1st citation represented. Also the entire sentence connected to the citation is highlighted. we only want the number highlighted for the picker." Two related bugs in `paper-citations.js` — both rooted in how the per-page scan converted regex matches to rects.

### Bug Fixes
- **`rm/js/paper-citations.js`** — when the PDF text said `[1, 5, 9]`, `_matchedRef` only resolved the first number-run (`parseInt((match.inner.match(/\d+/) || [''])[0])`) and `refKey = m[1]` ("1, 5, 9") collapsed the whole cluster into one row. New `_expandNumericInner(inner)` helper splits clusters and numeric ranges into one `{ n, charStart, charEnd }` entry per ref (range `5–7` → entries for 5, 6, 7 all sharing the literal `5–7` char-span). `_scanPage`'s numeric branch now iterates the expansions and emits one match per ref number, each with `refKey = String(n)` so `_renderPanel`'s byKey dedup surfaces all three rows. `_matchedRef`'s numeric path simplified — `match.inner` is now always a single number.
- **`rm/js/paper-citations.js`** — flash-rect computation widened to entire pdf.js text-items that overlapped the regex match, so hovering a row flashed the whole sentence whenever the marker lived inside a sentence-sized text-run (which is most body-text PDFs). New `_rectForRange(ranges, rangeStart, rangeEnd)` slices each overlapping item by the character-fraction that actually overlaps `[rangeStart, rangeEnd]`. Both numeric and author-year branches now feed their match's char-span through it, so `[1,5,9]` → three thin rects, one per digit; `(Smith, 2020)` → just the marker, not the surrounding run. Approximation assumes roughly even glyph distribution within a text-item — fine for body text, degrades on kerned/justified runs, still vastly better than the whole-item rect.

### Changed
- **`sw.js`** — `CACHE_VERSION` 73 → 74.

### Notes
- Existing hover/click behavior is otherwise unchanged. `_renderPanel`'s `byKey` dedup keeps the same row count when the same ref appears in multiple clusters on the page (e.g. `[1,5,9]` and `[5]` still merge into one row for ref 5 with two `hits`). The `lp-cite-token` chip continues to show the original cluster token (`[1,5,9]`) rather than synthesizing a per-row `[5]` — the narrowed flash is what disambiguates which digit each row belongs to.
- **Hard-reload required** to evict SW cache `mcgheelab-shell-v74`.

## [V3.98] - 2026-05-08

**Surface papers + grants directly in the link-picker.** Reported: "on the Link this paper to a project bucket popup the only projects that show up on the linker are other. There are not grants and papers section." Root cause was structural — V3.95 grouped buckets by their linked item's `type`, but most user-created buckets in `tasks/buckets.json` carry `category: ''` and have no `linked_item_ids`, so they all fell into "Other". Many papers + grants in `items.json` had no bucket pinned at all, so they never appeared in the picker.

### Changed
- **`rm/js/paper-overlays.js`** — `_openLinkPicker` now shows three sections of *rows*, not just buckets:
  - **Papers** — every `type: 'paper'` item from `items.json` (excluding the open paper itself). For each, the row resolves to the first bucket linked to that paper (if any), or is a *virtual* row that auto-creates a bucket on save.
  - **Grants** — every `type: 'grant'` item, same treatment.
  - **Other** — free-form buckets and any buckets linked to non-paper / non-grant items (research projects, courses, etc.). Buckets surfaced in Papers/Grants are excluded so each appears exactly once.
  - Auto-create uses the existing `LINKS.pinItemToDashboard(item)` helper, which calls `newProjectForItem` under the hood — bucket title verbatim matches the item title (`item.title || item.name || idStem`).
- **`rm/js/paper-overlays.js`** — virtual rows render with a yellow `will create` badge so the user knows clicking will instantiate a bucket. Each row carries a muted hint line: "Smith 2024 · Journal" for papers (extracted from `meta.library.authors[0]` / `meta.library.year` / `meta.library.journal`) and "Agency · Grant Number" for grants. The hint is searchable.
- **`rm/js/paper-overlays.js`** — modal gains a search input that filters rows live across all three sections. Section count chips reflect filtered totals; sections collapse when fully filtered out. Auto-focuses on open. Helps when a lab has dozens of papers in `items.json`.
- **`rm/js/paper-overlays.js`** — save handler rewritten in two passes: (1) resolve every checked row to a concrete bucket id, calling `pinItemToDashboard` only for virtual item rows that lack a bucket; (2) diff against the open paper's existing linked-bucket set and fire `LINKS.addLink` / `LINKS.removeLink` for the delta. Idempotent for papers/grants that already have a bucket.
- **`rm/css/style.css`** — `#lp-linkpick-search` styles, `.lp-linkpick-search-wrap` wrapper, `.lp-linkpick-titlewrap` two-line row layout (title + hint), `.lp-linkpick-hint` muted metadata, `.lp-linkpick-badge` for the "will create" indicator.
- **`sw.js`** — `CACHE_VERSION` 72 → 73.

### Notes
- **Self-link prevented**: the open paper's own item is filtered out of the Papers section so the user can't accidentally link a paper to itself.
- **Item hint extraction is best-effort.** Papers often have full metadata under `meta.library`; grants vary in field naming (`meta.agency` / `meta.sponsor` / `meta.funder`, `meta.grant_number` / `meta.award_number` / `meta.proposal_number`). Empty hint just hides the second line — no crash.
- **The `+ Create + link` inline form below the list** still creates a free-form bucket linked to the open paper only — this is the path for buckets that don't tie to a specific paper or grant in `items.json` (e.g., a one-off review pass with a custom title).
- **Multiple buckets per item**: when a paper or grant has more than one bucket linked to it, only the first appears in its Papers/Grants row. Extras still show up in Other. A future enhancement could surface all of them (out of scope here).
- **Hard-reload required** to evict SW cache `mcgheelab-shell-v73`.

## [V3.97] - 2026-05-08

**Delete paper from library (with full cascade).** Reported: "we also need a way to delete papers from the library." Until now there was no in-UI way to remove a paper; mistaken imports, duplicates, and obsolete entries had to be cleaned up by hand in the Firebase console — and even that left orphan PDF blobs and orphan `evidence.item_ids` refs on tasks across all users.

### Added
- **`functions/library.js`** (new) — HTTPS endpoint `deletePaper({itemId})`. CORS allowlist + bearer-token auth match the existing pattern in `functions/scrape-now.js`. The handler runs the full cascade under the Admin SDK in this order: (1) verify caller is an admin (`users/{uid}.role === 'admin'`) OR the original uploader (case-insensitive email match against `items/{itemId}.meta.library.pdf.uploaded_by`); (2) delete the Storage blob at `meta.library.pdf.storage_path` with `{ignoreNotFound:true}`; (3) `db.recursiveDelete(papers/{itemId})` cleans `annotations`, `yjs_snapshot`, `yjs_updates`, `presence`, `snapshots`, `comments`, and the doc itself in one call; (4) collection-group scan of every user's `userData/{uid}/tasks/*`, walking project/bucket/subtask/children trees to prune `itemId` from every `evidence.item_ids[]` and write back only docs that changed; (5) delete `items/{itemId}` last so partial upstream failures don't leave a row pointing at half-deleted state. Idempotent — calling on a missing item still mops up orphan `papers/{id}/*` subcollections and returns `{ok:true, alreadyMissing:true}`. Returns `{ok, itemId, blobDeleted, tasksScanned, tasksUpdated}` for client telemetry.
- **`functions/index.js`** — registers the new `deletePaper` export.
- **`rm/js/library.js`** — new `_canDelete(it)` visibility gate (admin-any OR caller email matches `lib.pdf.uploaded_by`); `_renderRow` appends a 🗑 button with `data-act="delete-paper"` after `Send` when `_canDelete` is true; `_onTableClick` gains a `delete-paper` branch that runs `confirm()`, fetches with `Authorization: Bearer <idToken>` against `https://us-central1-mcgheelab-f56cc.cloudfunctions.net/deletePaper`, prunes from `_items`/`_libraryPapers`, re-renders, and toasts on success/failure.

### Changed
- **`sw.js`** — `CACHE_VERSION` 71 → 73.

### Notes
- **Storage rules untouched.** `storage.rules` at `papers/{paperId}/{=**}` has no client `delete` rule by design; the Admin SDK in the Cloud Function bypasses Storage rules, so we don't loosen client-side guarantees just to enable deletion.
- **firestore.rules untouched.** The `items` collection still allows `write: if isLabMember()` (so direct SDK deletes by lab members are technically still possible). The Cloud Function is the authoritative path — UI gates the button to admin/uploader, server re-checks. Tightening to admin-or-uploader-only would need an `isOwner()` predicate and is left as a separate change.
- **Why a tasks scan instead of a Firestore index.** `evidence.item_ids` lives at multiple nested levels inside every tasks doc (project, bucket, subtask, recursive subtask children). Firestore does not index inside arrays of objects, so an `array-contains` query is impossible — we walk the tree. Per-user task collections are tiny (typically <50 docs/user), so a full collection-group read on delete is acceptable for an action that fires at most a few times per day.
- **Hard-reload required** to evict SW cache `mcgheelab-shell-v73`.
- **Deploy step**: `firebase deploy --only functions:deletePaper` from the repo root before the UI button works in production.

## [V3.94] - 2026-05-08

**Link a paper to a project bucket from the paper reader.** Reported: "the overlays says: No project buckets are linked to this paper yet. … I need a way to add the paper to a project bucket. how do I load in the AI highlighting and commenting done by claude." Until now the only way to link was via the projects/dashboard page (`unlinkBucketFromItem`) — context-switching from the reader was disruptive, and the empty-state copy pointed users somewhere else for what felt like an inline action.

### Changed
- **`rm/js/paper-overlays.js`** — overlays popover gains a `+ Link to project…` button (visible whether buckets are linked or not). Click opens a modal listing every existing project bucket with a checkbox; checked = linked. Saving uses `LINKS.addLink` / `LINKS.removeLink` for the diff. Footer of the modal has an inline "+ Create + link" form: type a title, click button, a fresh bucket is created (shape matches `LINKS.newProjectForItem`) and pre-linked to the open paper. After save, the popover re-fetches linked buckets, prunes/adds entries to the active set, and re-renders so the overlays checklist reflects reality immediately.
- **`rm/js/paper-overlays.js`** — empty-state copy rewritten to be self-serve: instead of "Pin it to a dashboard project (or use Send-to-teammate)" it says "Link one and AI overlays (drag-drop a `.paper-overlay.md` file) will scope to it." Plus the new link button below.
- **`rm/css/style.css`** — `.lp-overlays-link-btn` (purple primary), `.lp-linkpick-list/-row/-row-linked/-title/-id`, `.lp-linkpick-create` (input + button row), `.lp-linkpick-empty`. Reuses the existing `.lp-oim-card` modal frame from the overlay-import flow so the two modals match visually.
- **`sw.js`** — `CACHE_VERSION` 68 → 69.

### How the AI-overlay flow now works end-to-end

1. **Open the paper** in `library-paper.html` (it must already exist in the library).
2. **Click "Overlays" in the right toolbar → "+ Link to project…"** — link to (or create) the bucket your review task lives under, e.g. `proj-gels-...` for GELS aim 2.
3. **In your VSCode literature-review repo, run `/paper-overlay`** (the skill at `.claude/skills/paper-overlay/SKILL.md`). Claude writes a `<slug>.paper-overlay.md` with frontmatter (`paper_id`, `bucket_id`, `overlay_title`) + `## Highlight` blocks.
4. **Drag-drop the `.md` onto the paper reader.** `paper-overlay-import.js` parses it, validates that the quotes appear in the paper text, shows a preview modal with matched / unmatched counts. Confirm imports. If the bucket isn't already linked, it auto-links (so step 2 is optional — you can do it via the .md file too).
5. **The highlights now live in Firestore** with `bucket_ids: [bucketId]` and render under that overlay's color. Toggle the overlay on/off via the same overlays popover.
6. **Reopen the paper any time** — the highlights persist (they're annotations, not file-bound). The `.paper-overlay.md` was just the import vehicle.

### Notes
- **One paper, many buckets.** Linking is many-to-many. A paper can carry GELS highlights, MEBP highlights, and prostate-gels highlights simultaneously; the overlays popover toggles which sets render. Use `evidence_stance` in the .md to mark for/against on each highlight.
- **The .md file is ephemeral.** It's not stored on the bucket — only the parsed annotations are. If you want to re-import after editing the .md, just drag-drop it again; the importer dedupes by `(quote, page, bucket)` so re-imports are idempotent.
- **Hard-reload required** to evict SW cache `mcgheelab-shell-v69`.

## [V3.93] - 2026-05-08

**Parsed references are cached on the paper item + parsed at import time.** Reported: "the references that populate should be stored in context to the paper so that the next time it is loaded we don't have to do that again. Also when we import a new paper to the library this should be done as well." Previously every paper-reader open re-parsed the references list from scratch (~1–2 s), and import-time imports never parsed at all.

### Changed
- **`rm/js/paper-citations.js`** — references parser refactored so its core (`_parseRefsByPageRange`) accepts any item-collection callback. Existing in-viewer flow keeps using `_viewer.getTextItems`. New public `PAPER_CITATIONS.parseRefsFromAllItems(items)` lets callers pass pre-collected text items (e.g. from a background pdf.js text extraction). `init()` now short-circuits when `paperItem.meta.library.references` is already populated — the panel uses cached refs immediately and skips the parse + render-all wait. New `onCacheRefs(refs)` callback fires after a fresh parse so the host page can persist refs to the item.
- **`rm/js/library-paper.js`** — wires `onCacheRefs`: reloads `items.json`, finds the active paper, stamps `meta.library.references` (+ `references_parsed_at` date stamp + `references_parser_version: 'v3.93'` for future re-parse decisions), saves. Subsequent opens of the same paper use the cached array directly — no parse, no wait.
- **`rm/js/pdf-viewer.js`** — new public `PDF_VIEWER.extractTextItemsFromPdf(blobOrUrl)`. Loads the PDF via pdf.js, calls `page.getTextContent()` on every page (no canvas render, no DOM), converts each item to the `{text, x, y, width, height, page}` shape paper-citations expects. y-coordinates are flipped from PDF's bottom-left origin to top-down so existing line-grouping math works unchanged. Per-page items sorted by `(y asc, x asc)` since pdf.js streams text-content in stream order, not reading order.
- **`rm/js/library-upload.js`** — new public `LIBRARY_UPLOAD.parseAndCacheRefs(paperId, blob)`. Pipeline: extract text items via `PDF_VIEWER.extractTextItemsFromPdf` → `PAPER_CITATIONS.parseRefsFromAllItems` → save to `items.json` under `meta.library.references`. Best-effort: silently no-ops when either dependency is unloaded so other pages that load library-upload (e.g. the wishlist tooling) aren't broken. `fromDoi` fires this in the background after the OA PDF upload completes; the OA blob is already in memory so no extra fetch.
- **`rm/js/library.js`** — manual file-upload path (`_processFile`) now also fires `LIBRARY_UPLOAD.parseAndCacheRefs(item.id, file)` after the items.json save. Background, non-blocking — the toast still says "Added X" immediately; the references quietly land on the item a few seconds later.
- **`rm/pages/library.html`** — papers tab now also loads `paper-citations.js` (so `parseRefsFromAllItems` is exposed) and `pdf-viewer.js` as a module (for `extractTextItemsFromPdf`). paper-citations registers `window.PAPER_CITATIONS` with no DOM side-effects until `init()` is called, which still only happens on the paper-reader.
- **`sw.js`** — `CACHE_VERSION` 67 → 68.

### Notes
- The new fields on `meta.library`: `references` (the parsed array), `references_parsed_at` (ISO date), `references_parser_version` (string). Existing items without these fields will get them on next paper-reader open. There's no migration step — the cache builds itself organically.
- **Failure mode**: when the parser can't find a heading (page range fallback exhausted), it returns `[]` and nothing is cached. Next open will retry. To force a re-parse after a parser improvement, bump `references_parser_version` and add an init-time check to invalidate older cached refs (not implemented yet — current behavior is "cache once, trust forever").
- **CORS-blocked OA PDFs**: when Unpaywall finds a publisher-hosted PDF that CORS blocks, `pdfBlob` stays null in `fromDoi`, no parse fires at import. Once the user opens the paper (with a manually-uploaded PDF) the V3.93 first-open parse + cache covers them.
- **Hard-reload required** to evict SW cache `mcgheelab-shell-v68`.

## [V3.92] - 2026-05-08

**Two complaints, two fixes.** Reported: "the open pill and close pill are in different locations" and "the citations still don't work — when the paper is loaded we look at the references section of the paper to get the required data."

### Changed
- **`rm/js/shell-popouts.js` + `rm/css/workflow-shell.css`** — popout open/close pill is now a single element anchored at the viewport edge, regardless of state. Closed → vertical icon + label (32×120 floating tab). Open → chevron pointing inward (32×80, same x/y anchor). Mouse muscle-memory carries between toggle and back; previously the close pill sat on the popout's inner edge (~460px from the viewport) so users had to mouse across the popout to close it. Open popout reserves a 32px outer-edge gutter (`padding-left`/`padding-right` on `.shell-popout.open`) so the pill never covers iframe content. Retired the inner-edge `.shell-popout-toggle` button — the header × still closes if the user prefers center-of-panel close.
- **`rm/js/paper-citations.js`** — references-section heading detection rewritten to scan **joined-line text** instead of per-item text. Many PDFs render "REFERENCES" as one glyph per text-layer span; the previous per-item `REF_HEADING.test(item.text)` couldn't see the heading because no single span held the full word, so the parser silently returned `[]` and every citation rendered as "No matching reference parsed." New `_groupItemsIntoLines()` collapses items at similar y-coordinates on the same page into a single line entry, and the regex runs on the joined text. Page-range fallback escalates from last 25 → last 60 → entire document so long PDFs (and ones with appendices after the references list) still get parsed. Heading regex made case-insensitive and reworded to also match "Notes and References", "1. References", and similar prefixed forms; long lines (>60 chars) are excluded so prose paragraphs containing the word "references" don't false-match. Logs the matched line + page on success and the give-up reason on failure so future regressions are easier to diagnose.
- **`sw.js`** — `CACHE_VERSION` 66 → 67.

### Notes
- The paper-citations entry segmentation (numeric prefix at left margin, paragraph y-gap) is unchanged from V3.90 — only heading detection was the silent failure point.
- **Hard-reload required** to evict SW cache `mcgheelab-shell-v67`.

## [V3.91] - 2026-05-08

**Paper-reader side panels can be reopened after collapse.** Reported: "when i close the side context windows on the paper reader page they disappear forever because the chat and task side menus are on top of the context menu open and close pills." Root cause: the expand pill (visible only when the panel is collapsed) sat at `left:50%; top:50%` inside a 32px-wide collapsed strip pinned to the viewport edge — exactly where the shell-popout collapsed pill (32px wide, viewport-edge, `top:50%`, 120px tall) lives. The popout pill is in the parent shell's stacking context, so a higher z-index inside the iframe can't beat it; the only way out is to move the expand pill out of the popout pill's vertical zone. The collapse pill (visible when the panel is OPEN) is unaffected — it sits at the panel's inside edge, far from the viewport edge.

### Changed
- **`rm/css/style.css`** — `.lp-expand-left,.lp-expand-right` now positioned at `top:60px` (anchored near the top of the strip) instead of `top:50%`. The popout pill's vertical span is roughly viewport-center ± 60px, so a top-anchored expand pill is fully clear of it on any reasonable viewport. Inline comment explains why we depart from the matching collapse-pill position.
- **`sw.js`** — `CACHE_VERSION` 65 → 66.

### Notes
- Behavior unchanged when the page is opened OUTSIDE the workflow shell (e.g., direct `/rm/pages/library-paper.html` URL) — the expand pill is just slightly higher than before, no functional difference.
- **Hard-reload required** to evict SW cache `mcgheelab-shell-v66`.

## [V3.90] - 2026-05-08

**Citation panel actually shows reference metadata + auto-fetches OA PDFs on add.** V3.86 shipped the citations panel but: (a) the references parser was tripping on common journal styles so every token rendered as "No matching reference parsed", and (b) the "+ Add to library" button stub-created a paper item without the PDF, so adding a cited paper still left it in the no-PDF queue. Both fixed.

### Changed
- **`rm/js/paper-citations.js`** — references parser rewritten to walk text items in reading order rather than y-clustered "lines" (so two-column references aren't column-mixed), more permissive heading regex (matches `References:`, `1. References`, `References 45` page-number tail, etc.), entry segmentation now uses two strong signals — numeric prefix at left margin OR paragraph-level y-gap (>1.4 line heights) — instead of a fragile median-x heuristic. Entry metadata extraction now pulls **title** and **journal** in addition to DOI/year/first-author/arXiv. Two title-extraction styles: APA-ish `Authors. (YYYY). Title. Journal, …` and Vancouver-ish `[1] Authors. Title. Journal year; …`. Console-logs the parse outcome so you can see whether the heading was found.
- **`rm/js/paper-citations.js`** — citation panel display: each row now shows `<author> <year>` in bold + a truncated title preview in the head. Expanding a row reveals a labeled metadata table (Author / Title / Journal / DOI / arXiv) plus a `<details>` for the raw entry. **"✓ in library" chip** (clickable → opens the cited paper) renders inline in the row head when the parsed DOI or arXiv id matches an existing library entry. **"no id" chip** when neither is parsed (so the user knows there's nothing actionable). Action button is now context-aware: "Open paper →" when in library, "+ Add to library" when not but DOI is parsed, "+ Add (arXiv)" when only arXiv id is parsed (synthesized as a `10.48550/arXiv.<id>` DOI for the Crossref lookup).
- **`rm/js/library-upload.js`** — `fromDoi(doi)` now tries to fetch the OA PDF automatically. Workflow: Crossref metadata → Unpaywall lookup (`api.unpaywall.org/v2/<doi>?email=…` — CORS-friendly) → if `best_oa_location.url_for_pdf` is present, attempt `fetch(url, { mode: 'cors' })` → verify content-type and `%PDF` magic bytes → upload via existing `uploadPdf(item.id, blob)` path so the paper appears with a real `meta.library.pdf` block exactly like a manual upload. CORS-blocked URLs (most publisher domains) fall back to `meta.library.pdf_candidate_url` + `pdf_candidate_source` + `pdf_candidate_note` so the wishlist's "no-pdf-found queue" workflow has a starting point. Returns `{item, alreadyExisted, pdfInfo, pdfCandidateUrl, oaSource}` — the caller can show a richer success toast.
- **`rm/js/library-paper.js`** — `onLibraryChanged` callback now reloads `items.json` AND calls `PAPER_CITATIONS.refreshLibraryStatus()` so the citation row's chip flips to "✓ in library" + button flips to "Open paper →" the moment add succeeds. New `PAPER_CITATIONS.refreshLibraryStatus()` is a panel-only re-render (no text re-scan).
- **`rm/css/style.css`** — `.lp-cite-author` / `.lp-cite-title` / `.lp-cite-chip` / `.lp-cite-chip-lib` / `.lp-cite-chip-noid` / `.lp-cite-meta-row` / `.lp-cite-actions` / `.lp-cite-open` styles for the new richer citation card.
- **`sw.js`** — `CACHE_VERSION` 64 → 65.

### Notes
- **Unpaywall is CORS-friendly; PDF hosts are mostly not.** In practice the auto-fetch succeeds on arXiv, bioRxiv, medRxiv, PMC, and most institutional repositories; it CORS-fails on Elsevier, Wiley, Springer, ACS, Nature, IEEE etc. — which is why we save the URL as a candidate so the user can complete the loop manually (or via the planned no-PDF-queue tooling).
- **`pdf_candidate_url` is a new optional field on `meta.library`.** It does NOT trigger the paper-reader's "this paper has a PDF" code path (`storage_path` does). The citations panel's "Open paper →" button stays inert for candidate-only items until the user uploads the PDF.
- **`firestore.rules` not affected** — `items.json` writes go through the existing `lab` scope adapter.
- **arXiv-id-only references**: when only `arXiv:1234.5678` is parsed (no DOI), the panel synthesizes `10.48550/arXiv.1234.5678` as the DOI for the Crossref lookup. Crossref does index arXiv DOIs.
- **Hard-reload required** to evict SW cache `mcgheelab-shell-v65`.

## [V3.89] - 2026-05-08

**Popouts persist across workflow switches + page picker lists every page.** Reported: "when switching workflows, the side popouts both default to opened and they refresh. They should be loaded and stay loaded and their state should persist through anything we do in RM. Also the right popout menu does not have the correct dropdown to change the popout to a different page type."

### Three changes

#### 1. In-shell workflow switcher (popouts stay mounted)
Previously, switching workflows meant: shell → chooser (full page nav) → click another workflow card → shell again (another full page nav). Two reloads obliterated everything in the popouts.

- **`rm/js/nav.js`** — when `location.pathname === '/rm/pages/workflow-shell.html'`, the strip's brand becomes a hover-dropdown wrapper (`.ws-brand-dropdown`) instead of a plain anchor. Hover opens a menu listing all default workflows + the user's custom workflows + an "Open chooser…" footer.
- **`rm/js/nav.js`** — new `_wfPopulateBrandDropdown()` populates the menu after the workflow record loads. Pulls from `_wfDefaultsCache` + `_wfCustomCache`. Click a menu entry → dispatches `rm:shell:switch-workflow { workflowId, kind }`.
- **`rm/js/workflow-shell.js`** — listens for `rm:shell:switch-workflow`. Reconfigures in-place: `WorkflowState.setActive(id, kind)`, `replaceState` to update `?workflow=` + clear `?active=`, fetches the new workflow record, picks a landing page, calls `showActiveFrame(landing)` (lazy-creates a new iframe; old workflow's iframes stay mounted under `display: none` in the `_frames` map for instant return), refreshes the strip via `_wfRefreshStrip()`. **No page navigation occurs**, so the popouts (their iframes, scroll positions, in-progress edits) are untouched.
- **`rm/css/workflow.css`** — `.ws-brand-dropdown` + `.ws-brand-menu` + `.ws-brand-menu-item` styles. Hover-to-open like the regular `.nav-dropdown` pattern.

#### 2. Popout state persists in localStorage
URL is no longer the only source of popout state. Workflow switch via the chooser still works (full nav) and now restores the user's last popout config from localStorage.

- **`rm/js/shell-popouts.js`** — `readPersistedState()` / `writePersistedState()` read/write `localStorage['mcgheelab.shellPopout.state']` containing `{ leftPopout, rightPopout, leftOpen, rightOpen }`. `readState()` precedence is URL > localStorage > defaults. `writeState()` writes to BOTH URL and localStorage. So opening/closing a popout, swapping a page in a popout, or picking a different default page all stick across navigations and even browser restarts.

#### 3. Page picker lists every accessible page (grouped)
Was: workflow page IDs + chat + tasks. Many pages weren't reachable as a popout target.

- **`rm/js/shell-popouts.js`** — picker now uses `<optgroup>` sections: "This workflow" (workflow's pageIds), "Quick" (chat / tasks defaults if not already shown), then every other accessible page in `PAGE_REGISTRY.list` bucketed by NAV section (Activity / Research / Operations / Lab Admin / Settings / Other). `firebridge.canAccessPage` filter applied throughout.

### Other
- **`sw.js`** — `CACHE_VERSION` 63 → 64.

### Notes
- **Popout iframe persistence** is now true within a shell session (workflow switch via brand dropdown). Across the chooser route (full page nav), the iframe re-creates but at least its open/closed + page selection are restored from localStorage so the visible state matches the user's prior session.
- **Memory cost of in-shell workflow switching:** previous workflow's main iframes stay in DOM (`display: none`). Switching back is instant; cumulative footprint scales with how many distinct workflows the user visited in the session. Acceptable for typical 2–3 workflow sessions; could add LRU later if it bites.
- No firestore.rules / functions changes.
- **Hard-reload required** to evict SW cache `mcgheelab-shell-v64`.

## [V3.88] - 2026-05-08

**Bug fix — split panes showed nested workflow nav inside each iframe.** Reported: "now the split pages have their own workflow nav on each page header."

### Root cause

When the user clicked `⊟ Split` from inside the workflow shell, the strip's pre-fill code in `nav.js` set `leftURL` to `location.pathname + location.search + location.hash`. On the workflow shell, that's `/rm/pages/workflow-shell.html?workflow=…&active=…`. The split's left iframe then loaded **the workflow shell itself** — which boots its own `workflow-shell.js`, renders its own popouts, and lazy-loads its own active-page iframe. The user saw a workflow shell nested inside each split pane.

### Fix
- **`rm/js/nav.js`** — when `location.pathname === '/rm/pages/workflow-shell.html'`, the strip's split-link `leftURL` is now the **active workflow page's URL** (looked up from `?active=` + `pageMap` + `state.pageState[active]` for resume URL). Outside the shell (split-view, individual pages), behavior is unchanged: `leftURL = location.pathname + .search + .hash`.
- **`sw.js`** — `CACHE_VERSION` 62 → 63.

### Notes
- **Effect:** clicking ⊟ Split from the shell now opens split-view with `left=/rm/pages/library.html?paper=mebp` (the actual page), not `left=/rm/pages/workflow-shell.html?…`. The iframe loads the page directly with `?embed=1` + `name=rm-embed-left` so nav.js inside suppresses both regular nav and workflow strip — clean panes.
- Cmd-click on a chip in shell mode still opens the chip's full URL in a new tab (no behavior change there — the href stays valid).
- No firestore.rules / functions changes.
- **Hard-reload required** to evict SW cache `mcgheelab-shell-v63`.

## [V3.87] - 2026-05-08

**Chat-in-popout cleanup.** User reported chat in the side popout was confusing — Overview took precedence over the actual conversation, clicking conversations didn't load reliably, page-title and bottom bars stole vertical space the popout doesn't have. Targeted fixes in chat.js for embed mode.

### Background

Chat renders a `mobile` layout when `window.innerWidth ≤ 700px` (Overview / Chat / Files / Search tabs, one section at a time). Popouts default to 460px wide so they always trip the mobile threshold. The mobile layout was designed for full-screen phones; in a sub-panel it carried two pieces of chrome (page-title top bar + cross-app bottom bar) that were redundant and ate ~80–100 px of vertical space, AND defaulted `_mobileTab` to `overview` so users always landed on the channel list instead of the conversation they wanted to read.

### Changed
- **`rm/js/chat.js`** — `_IS_EMBED` constant computed once at module init from three signals: `window.parent !== window` (loaded inside an iframe), `window.name` matching `/^rm-(embed|shell)/` (set by V3.76 / V3.78 / V3.85 shell iframes), or `?embed=1` query (V3.73 fallback).
- **`rm/js/chat.js`** — `_mobileTab` default flips from `'overview'` to `'chat'` when `_IS_EMBED`. Users opening the chat popout land on their last conversation immediately; Overview is one tab tap away if they need to switch channels.
- **`rm/js/chat.js`** — `render()`'s mobile branch skips `renderMobileTopBarHTML()` and `renderMobileBottomBarHTML()` when `_IS_EMBED`. The popout's own header (page picker dropdown, close × button, drag-resize slider) handles "what is this" + "switch / close." Reclaims ~80 px of vertical space.
- **`rm/js/chat.js`** — `selectChannel(channelId)` now writes `localStorage['mcgheelab.chat.lastChannelId'] = channelId` on every selection. The channel-subscription bootstrap reads it and auto-picks that channel on first open if it still exists; falls back to the most-recent-activity channel as before. So reopening the chat popout returns to the same conversation across sessions.
- **`sw.js`** — `CACHE_VERSION` 61 → 62.

### Notes
- Embed-mode behavior is purely additive — chat outside a popout (full-page on `/rm/pages/chat.html`) keeps the original mobile / desktop layouts unchanged.
- `localStorage` last-channel persistence is per-browser, not synced across devices.
- No firestore.rules / functions changes.
- **Hard-reload required** to evict SW cache `mcgheelab-shell-v62`.

## [V3.86] - 2026-05-08

**Library paper reader gains four literature-review capabilities** — citations panel, project-bucket overlays, drag-drop `.paper-overlay.md` import, and highlight-aware in-paper search. Wishlist source: [rm/wishlist.md](../../rm/wishlist.md) lines 3–11. Plan: [V3.86_library_paper_overlays.md](../ClaudesPlan/V3.86_library_paper_overlays.md). Project buckets ([rm/js/links.js](../../rm/js/links.js)) are reused as the overlay key — no new entity invented.

### Added
- **`rm/js/paper-citations.js`** — left-sidebar "Citations on page N" panel. On `_viewer.ready()`, parses references from the back of the paper (heading match + hanging-indent split + DOI/year extraction). On every page change, regex-scans the page text for `[12]` numeric and `(Smith et al., 2020)` author-year tokens; renders one row per unique reference. Hover sidebar → flash on PDF; hover PDF token → highlight sidebar row. Expand row reveals full reference text + DOI link + **"+ Add to library"** button.
- **`rm/js/paper-overlays.js`** — overlay picker popover anchored at `#lp-overlays-anchor` in the right toolbar. Lists project buckets linked to this paper (`window.LINKS.linkedBucketsForItem`), each with a deterministic-color swatch + checkbox. All / None mini-buttons. State persisted at `localStorage.rm_lp_overlays_<paperId>`. Public API: `init`, `getActiveBucketIds`, `getFilterFn`, `getColorForBucket`, `getLinkedBuckets`, `onChange`.
- **`rm/js/paper-overlay-import.js`** — drag-drop a `.md` onto `#lp-viewer` to import highlights as bucket-scoped annotations. Banner appears on dragenter, modal on drop. Parser handles minimal YAML frontmatter (`paper_id` / `paper_doi`, `bucket_id`, `overlay_title`) + `## Highlight` blocks (`page`, `quote`, `color`, `comment` literal-block, `cite_in_drafts`, `evidence_stance`). Validation: paper-id strict-match, bucket existence (auto-link if not yet linked to paper), per-quote text-layer fuzzy-whitespace match. Preview modal lets the user de-select unmatched highlights; idempotent (skips existing `(quote, page, bucket)`).
- **`rm/js/paper-search.js`** — keyword search box at `#lp-search-anchor` in the right toolbar. Scans every page's text items, ranks hits inside existing highlight text-quotes first (page asc as tiebreak). Click a result → `_viewer.gotoPage(p)` + flash via `_flashRectOnPage`. Capped at 6 hits per page so a generic word doesn't return thousands.
- **`.claude/skills/paper-overlay/SKILL.md`** — Claude Code skill that authors `.paper-overlay.md` files in sibling VSCode lit-review repos (Prostate GELS, MEBP, MRI). Documents the format, behavior rules (verbatim quotes, lens-aware comments, no PII).
- **`rm/js/library-upload.js`** new `fromDoi(doi)` — looks up DOI via `LIBRARY_METADATA`, builds a paper item with no PDF, appends to `items.json`. Used by Phase 1's "+ Add to library" button. De-dupe by `meta.library.doi`.

### Changed
- **`rm/pages/library-paper.html`** — script tags for `links.js`, `paper-citations.js`, `paper-overlays.js`, `paper-overlay-import.js`, `paper-search.js`. New DOM slots: `<div id="lp-citations">` between `#lp-tags` and `#lp-metadata`; `<div id="lp-overlays-anchor">` and `<div id="lp-search-anchor">` as new toolbar rows.
- **`rm/js/library-paper.js`** — initializes each new module after `_mountViewer`; composes `PAPER_OVERLAYS.getFilterFn` AND with `ANNOTATION_PANEL.getFilterFn` in `_applyFilter`; stamps `bucket_ids: PAPER_OVERLAYS.getActiveBucketIds()` on new highlights via `ANNOTATION_OVERLAY.onCreate`; passes `getBuckets`/`getBucketColor`/`onBucketToggle` to `ANNOTATION_PANEL.init`; new helper `_flashRectOnPage(page, x, y, w, h)`; `_onPageChange` now also calls `PAPER_CITATIONS.refreshForPage(p)`; `onPageReady` callback also refreshes citations on the current page.
- **`rm/js/annotation-sync.js`** — `bucket_ids: []` added to create defaults so every annotation doc carries the field.
- **`rm/js/annotation-overlay.js`** — `_renderRectsForPage` now draws per-bucket left-edge stripes when `>1` overlay is active and the highlight has `bucket_ids`. Stripes are 3px wide, deterministic color from bucket id, only on the first rect of multi-line highlights.
- **`rm/js/annotation-panel.js`** — new optional opts `getBuckets`, `getBucketColor`, `onBucketToggle`; `_renderInfoPanel` grows an "Overlays" row of toggleable chips per linked bucket (orphan bucket ids in `bucket_ids` render as a non-clickable warning); chip click delegates to `onBucketToggle` (or falls back to a full `bucket_ids` patch via `onUpdate`).
- **`rm/css/style.css`** — styles for citations panel rows, overlay picker popover, per-bucket accent stripes + chips, drop banner, import modal, in-paper search results dropdown with `mark` highlighting.
- **`sw.js`** — `CACHE_VERSION` 60 → 61.

### Notes
- **Active-overlays state is localStorage, not Firestore.** Per-paper toggle state is ephemeral UI preference; per-paper Firestore prefs would be one read per paper open for no real benefit. (The plan-mode sketch had `paperPrefs` as a Firestore route; we simplified during implementation.)
- **`firestore.rules` was inspected, no edit required.** The annotations rule (line 505+) doesn't field-allowlist on owner writes — adding `bucket_ids` to a doc the creator owns just works. Non-creator updates are still restricted to `evidence_for_claim_ids`/`evidence_stance`/`modified` (the existing `hasOnly` clause), so non-owners can't change overlays on someone else's annotation. That's correct.
- **References parser is best-effort.** Numbered references with `[N]` or `N.` prefixes work cleanly; hanging-indent author-year lists work most of the time; column-broken references can split poorly. The cache key is `meta.library.references` on the paper item; if the parse looks wrong, hand-edit `items.json`.

## [V3.84] - 2026-05-08

**Bug fix — close pill on chat popout reloaded the iframe instead of closing the popout.** Reported: "when I click on the close chat popout, it just reloads the chat page and doesn't close the popout."

### Root cause

`writeState()` in workflow-shell.js only included `leftOpen` / `rightOpen` in the URL when truthy. On close:
1. `togglePopout(side, false)` → `writeState(s)` → URL drops the `leftOpen` param entirely
2. `renderPopout(side)` → `readState()` → URL has no `leftOpen`
3. V3.80's `readState` defaults missing `leftOpen` to **true** (so first-time visits open the popouts)
4. `renderPopout` sees `isOpen = true` → tears down + rebuilds the panel as if it's still open → new iframe gets a fresh src → chat reloads from scratch

The "default to open when missing" rule and "remove from URL when falsy" rule together made the close-state unrepresentable in the URL.

### Fix
- **`rm/js/workflow-shell.js`** — `writeState()` now ALWAYS writes `leftOpen` and `rightOpen` as literal `0` / `1` in the URL. Distinguishes "explicitly closed" (`0`) from "never visited" (param absent → still defaults to open).
- **`sw.js`** — `CACHE_VERSION` 58 → 59.

### Notes
- Click `×` in the panel header OR the chevron pill in the middle of the slider — both close the popout cleanly now.
- The pill at the viewport edge re-opens it (URL flips to `=1`); chat iframe is recreated on re-open (separate optimization to keep the iframe alive across toggle is queued).
- No firestore.rules / functions changes.
- **Hard-reload required** to evict SW cache `mcgheelab-shell-v59`.

## [V3.83] - 2026-05-08

**Bug fix — chip clicks in the workflow shell didn't switch pages.** Reported by user: "when I'm in a workflow, I can't switch pages." Root cause: a race between two writers of `?active=` in the URL.

### Root cause

V3.78's nav.js chip handler in shell mode did this on click:
1. `history.replaceState(...)` to set `?active=<newPageId>` on the URL
2. dispatch `rm:shell:set-active`
3. `_wfRefreshStrip()`

workflow-shell.js's listener then did:
```
const s = readState();   // reads URL — already has the NEW pageId
if (pageId === s.active) return;
```

So the listener early-bailed because `?active=` was already updated, and `showActiveFrame()` never ran → iframe never swapped → user clicks did nothing visible.

### Fix
- **`rm/js/nav.js`** — in shell-mode click handler, removed the URL `replaceState`. The listener in workflow-shell.js owns URL state via its own `writeState()` (which also dispatches `rm:split:state-change` listeners). CustomEvent dispatch is synchronous, so by the time `_wfRefreshStrip()` runs after `dispatchEvent`, the listener has already updated the URL and showActiveFrame has flipped the iframe; strip's chip-active class then reads the new `?active=` and lights up the right pill.
- **`sw.js`** — `CACHE_VERSION` 57 → 58.

### Notes
- Single source of truth: workflow-shell.js owns `?active=`. nav.js dispatches user intent.
- No firestore.rules / functions changes.
- **Hard-reload required** to evict SW cache `mcgheelab-shell-v58`.

## [V3.81] - 2026-05-08

**Workflow shell popouts are overlays now, not split panes.** V3.80 made the popouts flex items, which split the viewport into three columns (left popout / main / right popout). The user wanted FLOATING overlays so the main page never resizes — popouts slide in over the main content. Fixed by switching popouts to absolute positioning with a soft shadow.

### Changed
- **`rm/css/workflow-shell.css`** — `#shell-root` is now `position: relative` (not flex), and `#shell-main` is `position: absolute; inset: 0;` so main always fills the entire shell area regardless of popout state. `.shell-popout` is `position: absolute; top: 0; bottom: 0;` anchored to the appropriate edge with `z-index: 10`. When `.open`, the popout gets its width (default 460 px, user-resizable) + a soft drop shadow (`box-shadow: 0 0 24px rgba(15,23,42,.12)`) so the floating-layer affordance is visible. Wrapper is `pointer-events: none` when closed; pill + open panel are `pointer-events: auto` so they're clickable but don't block clicks on the main iframe.
- **Compact pill** (collapsed state) — was a full-height 40 px bar splitting the viewport. Now a small **32×120 px floating tab anchored at mid-height** on the appropriate edge, with rounded corners on the inner side and a small shadow. Hover slightly widens to 36 px for affordance. Vertical rotated label + icon. Replaces the V3.80 full-height pill so collapsed popouts don't visually take real estate from the main page.
- **`rm/css/workflow-shell.css`** — left popout pill: `border-radius: 0 10px 10px 0`; right popout pill: `border-radius: 10px 0 0 10px`. Borders flipped on `.open` state so the seam is on the appropriate side.
- **`sw.js`** — `CACHE_VERSION` 55 → 56.

### Notes
- **No JS changes** — the popout open/close + resize-drag + width persistence (V3.80) all still work; only the visual layout changed.
- **Trade-off**: when both popouts are open and total ≥ viewport width, they'll overlap each other visually. Acceptable on desktop (viewport > 1000 px is typical); mobile already has a separate overlay rule via the `@media (max-width: 800px)` breakpoint.
- **Hard-reload required** to evict SW cache `mcgheelab-shell-v56`.

## [V3.80] - 2026-05-08

**Workflow shell fixes — popout sizing + load order regression.** Three bugs reported on V3.78's shell; all fixed.

### Bugs fixed

#### 1. `[page-registry] NAV_ITEMS not in scope` — main page wasn't loading
- **`rm/pages/workflow-shell.html`** — V3.78 loaded `page-registry.js` BEFORE `nav.js`. page-registry.js reads `NAV_ITEMS` from nav.js's top-level scope, so it warned and bailed → `PAGE_REGISTRY` never built → `workflow-shell.js` couldn't render anything → blank page. Swapped the order: nav.js → page-registry.js → workflow-state.js → workflow-shell.js. Comment in HTML flags the dependency.

#### 2. Popouts didn't show by default
- **`rm/js/workflow-shell.js`** — `readState()` previously defaulted `leftOpen` / `rightOpen` to `false`, so chat + tasks were collapsed pills on every shell entry and the user had to click them to see anything. Defaults now flip to `true` (open) on first load — chat shows on the left, tasks on the right, immediately. URL params still override (so `?leftOpen=0` collapses on entry).

#### 3. Popouts too small + couldn't be resized
- **`rm/js/workflow-shell.js`** — bumped `DEFAULT_POPOUT_WIDTH` 380 → **460 px** for actual usability (chat + task lists need real width).
- **`rm/js/workflow-shell.js`** — added a per-side **drag-to-resize handle** on the popout's inner edge (right edge of left popout; left edge of right popout). Pointer-down on the handle starts a drag; pointermove updates the popout's width inline; pointerup persists the final width to `localStorage` under `mcgheelab.shellPopout.<side>Width` (clamped 240–900 px). Iframe pointer events are suppressed during the drag so the iframe doesn't capture the pointermove (same trick `split-view.js` uses for the divider).
- **`rm/js/workflow-shell.js`** — `applyPopoutWidth(side)` reads the saved width on render and applies it inline. `readPopoutWidth(side)` falls back to the default + clamps; persisted width survives page reloads, workflow switches, and across devices (well — `localStorage` is per-browser; cross-device sync would require Firestore — out of scope).
- **`rm/css/workflow-shell.css`** — `.shell-popout.open` now `position: relative` so the absolute-positioned resize handle anchors correctly. `.shell-popout-resize` rules: 6 px wide, full-height, `cursor: col-resize`; turns subtle blue on hover or while dragging. `body.shell-popout-resizing` suppresses iframe pointer events.

### Other
- **`sw.js`** — `CACHE_VERSION` 54 → 55.

### Notes
- **`localStorage` (not session)** for popout width — admin's preferred size sticks across browser restarts. URL still owns ephemeral state (which page is in each slot, whether each is open).
- **No firestore.rules / functions changes.**
- **Hard-reload required** to evict SW cache `mcgheelab-shell-v55`.

## [V3.78] - 2026-05-07

**Workflow shell — every workflow page is always loaded, with side popouts.** Two coupled features the user asked for:

1. **All workflow pages stay loaded.** Entering a workflow now lands the user on a single shell page (`rm/pages/workflow-shell.html`); each workflow page becomes an iframe inside it. The first chip click on a not-yet-visited page lazy-creates that iframe; subsequent visits to any chip just toggle DOM visibility (no reload, no data refetch). State (paper id, scroll, in-progress edits) survives chip switching.
2. **Side popouts.** Two collapsible panels (left + right) hugging the edges of the shell. Each is a small vertical pill (40px wide) when collapsed; clicking opens a 380px-wide panel with an iframe of the user's chosen page. Defaults: **left = Chat, right = Tasks**. A small dropdown in each popout's header swaps the page in that slot. URL persists `?leftPopout`, `?rightPopout`, `?leftOpen`, `?rightOpen`.

Cross-iframe consistency: handled by Firestore's existing live-sync (LIVE_SYNC.attach in each renderer) — when iframe A writes, iframe B's listener fires the same way it does for cross-tab updates. No new state-coordination machinery was needed.

### Added
- **`rm/pages/workflow-shell.html`** — single-page host for an entire workflow. Top: workflow strip (rendered by nav.js, shell-aware). Body: `#shell-popout-left` / `#shell-main` / `#shell-popout-right` row.
- **`rm/js/workflow-shell.js`** (~280 LOC) — orchestrates iframe lifecycle:
  - `readState()` / `writeState()` — single source of truth in URL: `?workflow=<id>&active=<pageId>&leftPopout=<pageId>&rightPopout=<pageId>&leftOpen=<0|1>&rightOpen=<0|1>`.
  - `loadWorkflow(id)` — Firestore (`labConfig/defaultWorkflows`) → seeds (PAGE_REGISTRY.DEFAULT_WORKFLOWS) → `userData/{uid}/customWorkflows/{id}` fallback chain.
  - `ensureFrame(pageId)` — lazy-creates an iframe for a workflow page, sets `name="rm-shell-<pageId>"` (V3.76 mechanism extended to also recognize `rm-shell-` prefix in nav.js suppression — already covered by the `rm-embed` prefix check).
  - `showActiveFrame(pageId)` — flips `display` between iframes; first-time activation creates the iframe.
  - `renderPopout(side)` — collapsed pill or open panel + iframe. Page picker dropdown lets the user pick which page goes in this slot. Restricted to workflow pages + chat/tasks (always available).
  - Listens for `rm:shell:set-active` events from the strip's chip clicks.
- **`rm/css/workflow-shell.css`** (~150 LOC) — vertical body flex; `#shell-root` horizontal flex with two popouts hugging edges; `.shell-popout-pill` (collapsed vertical bar with rotated label); `.shell-popout-header` + `.shell-popout-frame` (open state). Mobile fallback: open popouts overlay the main pane.

### Changed
- **`rm/js/nav.js`** — `renderWorkflowStrip` detects shell mode (`location.pathname === '/rm/pages/workflow-shell.html'`). In shell mode:
  - Active chip is determined by `?active=<pageId>` (not pathname/tab matching).
  - Chip click is captured (`e.preventDefault()`) and dispatches `rm:shell:set-active { pageId }`. URL updated via `history.replaceState`. Strip refreshes via `_wfRefreshStrip` so the active class moves.
  - Suppression check (`window.name`) already accepts the `rm-shell-` prefix because the existing check uses `indexOf('rm-embed') === 0` — needs an update? Actually no, the V3.76 check is `indexOf('rm-embed') === 0` which won't match `rm-shell-*`. **This file's renderNav embed-suppression line 357 needs to also accept `rm-shell-` prefix** — fixed in this commit by using a generic 'rm-' prefix detection (`/^rm-(embed|shell)-/.test(window.name)`).
- **`rm/js/workflow-chooser.js`** — both default-card and custom-card click handlers route through the workflow shell (`/rm/pages/workflow-shell.html?workflow=<id>&active=<landingPageId>`) instead of the landing page directly.
- **`sw.js`** — `CACHE_VERSION` 52 → 53.

### Notes
- **No firestore.rules / functions changes.** Workflow shell uses existing data paths (`labConfig/defaultWorkflows`, `userData/{uid}/customWorkflows`, `users/{uid}.allowedPageIds`).
- **Memory cost** — each iframe is ~5MB. Typical workflow has 5–7 pages, so peak footprint is ~25–35MB beyond the parent. Manageable on modern devices.
- **First-paint cost** — only the landing iframe loads on shell entry. Other iframes lazy-load on first chip click. Subsequent chip clicks are instant.
- **Direct page links from outside the shell** (e.g., a deep link to `/rm/pages/library.html`) still work and bypass the shell. Workflow context is preserved via sessionStorage if the user previously entered a workflow.
- **Split view** still works as before. From inside the shell, the strip's `⊟ Split` button takes the user to `split-view.html` (leaves the shell). No nested shell-in-split or split-in-shell — out of scope.
- **Hard-reload required** to evict SW cache `mcgheelab-shell-v53`.
